handbook.char_393_toledo.story.2.text.text: Claims to be a descendant of an Iberian Royal Navy admiral and a member of the fallen noble house, the De Toledo family, having gathered a large following across Iberia. However, due to severe discrepancies between her oral accounts and the Inquisition's archived records, her occupation was reclassified as a freelancer upon registration with Human Resources. De Toledo joined Rhodes Island under the recommendation of Operator Irene. Her eloquence and knowledge of Iberia are sufficient to assist operators in the Iberian Affairs Office with basic operations.

handbook.char_393_toledo.story.3.text.text:
Imaging tests reveal clear, normal outlines of internal organs, and no abnormal shadows detected. Originium granules detected in the circulatory system show no anomalies. There are no signs of Oripathy infection, confirming the subject as non-infected.

[Cell-Originium Assimilation] 0%
Operator De Toledo shows no signs of Originium infection.

[Blood Originium Crystal Density] 0.12u/L
Operator De Toledo has had very little contact with Originium, but her physical exam report still indicates multiple abnormal metrics: dehydration, anemia, chronic malnutrition... It can be inferred that her past travels wandering across Iberia were exceedingly harsh. The Medical Department will continue to monitor her basic health condition.

"...I naturally understand that your medical records are private personal data, and we will archive them according to standard procedures, but requesting to encrypt this report seems a bit..."
"No, no, no, you don't get it at all. As a noble, I can't let anyone—especially my followers—know that I suffer from malnutrition! Who'd want to follow a leader who can't even feed herself? Wait a minute... Could this actually be a new angle? Sacrificing her own well-being so her followers can live good lives... Doesn't that sound even more popular with the people? Alright then, no encryption needed!"

handbook.char_393_toledo.story.4.text.text:
[Operator De Toledo Archive Record]
Archive File 1
Current Process Status: Not Archived
Note: HR personnel are requested to expedite the background check and verify the authenticity of all Operator De Toledo's records. If special circumstances arise, an interview with the operator or relevant individuals may be conducted to confirm details verbally.

Archive File 1
Current Process Status: Returned
Note: I understand that compiling three separate six-hour oral interview recordings is difficult, but raw audio files simply do not meet the archive submission standards. Furthermore, please ensure that grandiose expressions such as "Conquerors of the Seas, the Glorious De Toledo Family" are omitted when transcribing into documentation.

Archive File 1
Current Process Status: Returned Again
Note: Per protocol, the background check should have been completed three months ago—well, my dear HR operator, you have my sympathies. Getting Tefi to utter a single truthful word about her background is indeed a formidable challenge.
Reply: Senior... Who is Tefi?
Reply: Operator De Toledo's nickname. Strange, did you not hear her mention it over these past four months? Wait, you haven't heard her recount "Rhea-Iberia and the Guests from the Deep"? What about "An Officer's Last Snowy Night"?
Reply: Huh...?

It was the first time in my life I had ever heard a speech so passionate, moving, and completely off-the-wall. Operator De Toledo stood at the center of the rec room's sunken lounge, sharing three stories with operators unfamiliar with Iberia and patients undergoing treatment at Rhodes Island. To be honest, she sounded like an utter fraud; perhaps only the children in the front row holding toy sailboats and paper badges were truly fooled. By the way, there are still far too few seats in the rec room—standing for three hours straight is terrible for the back. Fine, I admit I was somewhat moved by this boisterous Liberi myself, to the point of reaching for my wallet when she appealed for "Golden Fleet Preparation Funds." In all fairness, it wasn't really being taken. Like me, most listeners were probably stirred by her Iberian tales rather than actually believing she was some grand noble. Besides, she seems quite good to her followers—she even handled all the sound effects for her speech herself without making them do it.
Regrettably, after three hours, I still had no idea which parts of Operator De Toledo's story were true. I may never be able to complete her archival documentation. But I believe I did figure one thing out—I am not suited to be an HR operator who records and verifies facts. I ought to pursue the creative dream I abandoned long ago. I will join De Toledo's crew as a clerk to write stories for her. When the next HR operator arrives to verify her file, perhaps I will be able to tell them who De Toledo truly is.
—Resignation attachment, from a former HR operator

handbook.char_393_toledo.story.5.text.text:
When Operator De Toledo returns to Rhodes Island with her followers after completing missions for the Iberian Office, they refer to themselves as the "Rhodes Island Auxiliary Navy" and patrol the landship.
Though called a patrol, it resembles sightseeing more than anything. De Toledo refers to the operator dormitories as her "palace," the convalescent garden as her "royal garden," and the Engineering Department as her "armaments factory," drawing no small amount of criticism. De Toledo pays little mind to the opinions around her. She orders children accustomed to sleeping on damp Iberian floors to lie upon her own soft mattress; she escorts critically ill elders to the garden to smell floral scents absent from the seaside; and as for those timid young folks capable of building sturdy contraptions, De Toledo shoves them straight into the Engineering Department. Three days later, those youths and the Engineering operators all have glowing eyes, introducing newly invented equipment even more garrulously than she does. Over time, complaints about De Toledo's domineering antics vanished just as the letters accusing her of hogging the rec room did. Anyone who has interacted with her comes to realize that De Toledo acts just as much as she speaks—and given how endlessly she talks, what she does for her followers is enough to make one temporarily forget that her "followers" are actually "victims" taken in by her scheme—

Victims? I don't understand... Lady De Toledo isn't a storm, so how could we be "victimized" by her? I followed Her Ladyship all the way here from Scaleridge Town with nothing to my name. Her Ladyship put me in charge of cooking, having me boil seaweed soup for everyone. Of course, we couldn't always gather enough seaweed, so we'd mix in a little sand. She said once she found a reliable benefactor or got her own estate, she'd bring us all over to drink soup made of pure seaweed. I know this isn't Her Ladyship's home, but I received soup in a place filled with tables and chairs. Lady De Toledo did not deceive me. What? Her identity? Sometimes she really doesn't act like a noble, but none of us know what an Iberian noble is supposed to look like anyway, do we? If those noble lords already rotting in the dirt could be like Her Ladyship, that'd be wonderful. Ah, I remember now! Some followers questioned her before, and she proved her noble bloodline to us. Naval uniform? No, not that. Did you know she has eleven toes?
—A follower of De Toledo, an ordinary Iberian elder, stopping an archivist to speak

handbook.char_393_toledo.story.6.text.text:
"On the De Toledo Family Lineage and Eleven Toes"
Esteban Enriques De Toledo, an Iberian Royal Navy admiral during the Golden Age, possessed a steadfast character and immense pride. An outstanding helmsman and navigator, he was hailed by Iberians of his time as "De Toledo the Wave-Turner." Across his eighty-three years of life, he spent nearly seventy at sea. No matter how severe the storm threatening his vessel, he would stand at the fore of the deck. Countless sailors looked up to him as a role model, and extreme emulation drastically raised both mortality and promotion rates among sailors at the time.
However, after the Profound Silence, Rhea-Iberia sank, and extensive records regarding the royal family and nobility were lost. Word-of-mouth recollections and sparse remaining documents revealed a lesser-known side of this noble. Esteban Enriques De Toledo suffered from hereditary polydactyly. Deformed extra toes caused him to limp on flat land, whereas the pitching of a ship conveniently disguised his physical flaw. His navigational mastery may have been an innate talent, or perhaps the result of arduous effort to cover his disability for the sake of his pride.
The same tragedy befell his offspring. His heir, Estanislao, became a brilliant naval admiral; had the Profound Silence not occurred, he too would have spent his life at sea like his father. Rumor has it that when the Profound Silence struck, he leaped from his ship and limped out of Rhea-Iberia, vanishing without a trace ever since.
Today, Estefania Colon De Toledo, claiming to be the great-granddaughter of Esteban Enriques De Toledo, has re-emerged. Both her naval uniform and her eleven toes serve to attest to her identity. We ought to follow in her footsteps and revive the glory of the Iberian Royal Navy...

[A note tucked between book pages]
I didn't expect that after resigning from HR, the first task De Toledo assigned me would be writing her biography. Well, there have always been plenty of followers who doubted her noble origin. Most of the above content was extracted from the stories she told and strung back together logically. I am quite certain De Toledo is not a descendant of that great naval admiral, but I am indeed curious whether she truly has eleven toes, and if not, how she managed to deceive the followers seeking proof. Four days after the question arose, I found the answer in another story she told. Perhaps it is yet another tale she spun based on Iberian reality, but I shall record it for now:
There was once a poor Iberian woman whose husband was swallowed by the sea, leaving her to await childbirth alone. Due to a breech presentation, the infant's feet emerged first. That unfortunate child likewise suffered from polydactyly. The deeply devout woman believed she had birthed a Seaborn and fainted dead away. The child survived unharmed, but the woman took her own life. Raised by the villagers, the child was unable to perform manual labor due to her extra toes. She left the village, and her whereabouts thereafter remain unknown.

handbook.char_393_toledo.story.7.text.text:
[Field Operation Record from a Stationed Iberian Office Operator]
Before formally working with Operator De Toledo, I had quite a few reservations regarding her style. Leaving aside how she brings a grand entourage of followers wherever she goes and clears her throat to begin a speech at the sight of any small patch of open ground, before every mission, this restless Liberi vanishes completely. At times when I was uncertain whether such actions were appropriate according to Iberian customs, our nominal "guide" was practically nowhere to be seen.
Ever since Rhea-Iberia returned to the coastline and the Inquisition decided to lift the blockade, our work has become harder than ever. Legacy of the Golden Age is gradually returning to people's lives, and the faith of Iberians is undergoing a restructuring. Some citizens no longer blindly obey the doctrines issued by the Inquisition; meanwhile, those who shaped their lives around faith claim to have been "betrayed." On one occasion, a fasting Iberian actively refused our assistance, reciting old scripture to chase us away, so we left. Half an hour later, a furious De Toledo appeared before us.
That was the first time I had ever seen De Toledo angry. I had previously seen her wandering near that civilian's wooden hut; perhaps he was one of her prospective followers. But she simply handed me a list containing dozens of names, half of which were crossed off. She told me that one of her followers was the town's sugar distributor. Every afternoon, he would haul unrefined sugar from the sugarcane farm and deliver a little to everyone on the list. The wish he made to the great noble De Toledo was that he hoped he would no longer have to cross off names from that list.
The next day, De Toledo built a small podium outside that Iberian's door. On the third day, she spoke for ten consecutive hours. Just as the sun was about to dip below the ocean horizon, the Iberian inside the house replied to her. On the fourth day, she "blessed" the unrefined sugar using so-called "family maxims"—it was utterly absurd, yet that man licked a taste of sugar off the dish. With that, our relief mission came to a successful conclusion, and she gained a loyal follower.
On the way back to Rhodes Island, I apologized to her while congratulating De Toledo's crew on gaining another member. She didn't laugh and slap my arm like she usually did. She looked at the followers gathered around her; they called her the noblest person in Iberia, a title that previously belonged to the Saints of the Inquisition in their eyes.
I seem to understand what she was worried about. In an Iberia that remains turbulent, she needs to be "Noble De Toledo," and she needs to offer a choice to those Iberians who "suffered betrayal." Perhaps only when the majority of Iberians can place faith in themselves will she choose to deceive no longer.

handbook.char_393_toledo.story.8.text.text:
"Ahem... Minutes of the Third Joint Meeting between the De Toledo Naval Reserve and Rhodes Island..."
"Doctor, can this little gadget really record everything we say? Hey, wait, you didn't turn on the recording while I was secretly telling you the truth, did you?"
"Right, right, right! The recording is on now, and everything I'm saying is true, all of it!"
"Getting back to the point, this meeting is to report the general status of the preparations for the Naval Reserve I founded, funded by Rhodes Island."
"Personnel recruitment, nautical training, and weapon manufacturing are all progressing steadily with very bright prospects. I suggest increasing investment—hey, don't pull up the mission records!"
"..."
"Don't go silent on me! How does saving two children from human traffickers not count as personnel recruitment? How does rowing a boat to gather seaweed not count as nautical training? And as for weapon manufacturing—hand cannons and swords are only useful in the hands of Inquisition folks; our weapons should be plows and shovels!"
"I have to let my followers live good lives first before I can think about anything else. Trust me, I may deceive, but I never break a promise!"
"Doctor, you agree to increase the investment? There's a condition?"
"...Incorporate my experiences with my followers into the stories for your speeches?"
"Piece of cake! I promise you, you'll definitely be the very first listener!"

handbook.char_1015_aglna2.story.4.text.text:
Among Rhodes Island's field Operators, there is no shortage of individuals who have made significant accomplishments in the field of Arts, some of whom can even be called masters. But if you were to ask which Operator has shown the most remarkable progress during their tenure at Rhodes Island, the vast majority of field Operators who excel in Arts would bring up Angelina's name.
When Angelina first began participating in field work, Rhodes Island classified her as a Trainee Caster Operator, not wishing for her to bear too heavy a burden during field missions. However, Angelina's primary identity is not that of a Caster, but a messenger. She rarely stays at Rhodes Island for long periods, and even when she is aboard the landship, she is usually busy collecting and packing parcels, hardly ever finding a chance to take the Trainee Caster promotion test. As a result, she wore the moniker of "Trainee Caster Operator" for a very long time, until a schedule finally cleared up and she apprehensively took the promotion test—which subsequently induced a considerable amount of psychological pressure on the trainee operators who went after her.
Even though she passed the test smoothly, Angelina still felt that her Arts capabilities had many areas needing improvement, and she has been working hard toward that end—though one can hardly fault her for pursuing perfection, as the ability to exert influence over gravity is an exceedingly rare talent, and there was no one on Rhodes Island capable of guiding her hand-in-hand. Not only that, this type of Originium Arts is also extremely difficult to control, making it hard to achieve a 100% success rate, which in turn affected Angelina's accurate assessment of her own abilities.
Regardless, after this trip to Rim Billiton, Angelina was evidently much more confident than before. The person who experienced this most profoundly was none other than Croissant, who shares a close personal friendship with Angelina. The two of them often held "Arts vs. Brawn" weightlifting competitions; at first they only compared weight, but later, after Angelina's control over her Arts reached a new level, the two began competing to see who could lift the heaviest load with the utmost stability. Later still, Croissant could only occasionally turn the tables by relying on rules such as "balancing a small ball on top of an entire stack of suitcases without letting it drop," right up until this recent occasion...

No matter how heavy the object is, she can lift both the heavy object and me together right after I lift it! After that, no one will ever compete with her in weightlifting again, wuwu...
-- Croissant

That being said, when Angelina used her Arts to arrange heavy objects into a staircase in the air and invited Croissant to the highest point to take in the scenery, Croissant still enthusiastically accepted the invitation.

handbook.char_1015_aglna2.story.5.text.text:
Putting aside her level of Arts proficiency, Angelina's primary identity at Rhodes Island remains that of a Rhodes Island messenger.
There is actually not much we can say on this matter, and for good reason: a competent messenger does not leave behind much talking point. Packages delivered, letters sent, and the messenger's figure naturally fades away into the background. Yet, in their silence, messengers inevitably know many things—who sent a letter to whom, who received a letter and never replied, whose address keeps changing... Fragments of information like these alone are enough to piece together certain truths that are perhaps not particularly vague. Consequently, many messengers view silence—or at least silence at the appropriate juncture—as a virtue.
Messengers originating from Siracusa understand this principle better than anyone else, and Angelina is no exception. She is, of course, an ordinary young girl who will chat with her peers about fashion, trends, and styling, but she will also conceal and swallow her emotions on many occasions, letting those heart-pounding feelings slowly dry, weather, and turn into secrets she will never speak of again.
We have no intention of interfering with the messenger's way of working, but we do hope that Angelina can spend this unique period of her life in the way she truly desires, and the best support we can offer her is unconditional trust in her kindness and sense of responsibility.
She is clearly aware of this. She is now the most senior among the messengers who have long served Rhodes Island, ranking among the best in both the number of items sent and delivered and the completion rate of deliveries, and she is often able to offer her own insights on logistics matters. At the same time, she increasingly regards Rhodes Island as a place she can truly rely on, depend on, and be herself. She will decorate her dorm room to her liking, leave a small gift for the doctor after her physical exam, or, when feeling restless, walk into the game room in silence to play games for an entire day, or sit in the cafeteria and eat ice cream box after box at a restrained but uninterrupted pace.

So you really weren't using your Arts when you stepped on the scale?
-- Curious Thani

Who brings an Arts casting unit onto a scale?!
-- A helpless and exasperated Angelina

handbook.char_1015_aglna2.story.6.text.text:
Angelina's journey to Rim Billiton brought us, first and foremost, three new Operators with distinct personalities; second, data related to active Originium in southern Rim Billiton; and finally, some news related to Hilda's so-called followers.
However, those individuals occupied far too peripheral a position among her followers. One of them, after following Uluru away from Red Sand Town, made their way to a certain Rhodes Island office, where they spent the final days of their life. According to them, the most core members among them did not even dare claim they had ever seen Hilda.
During her subsequent travels passing through Rim Billiton, Angelina traced the origins of these individuals more than once, successfully piecing together the life stories and indoctrination experiences of some of them, but the vast majority of leads ultimately ended in dead ends.

[Privilege Log]
"That great traveler set out from Rim Billiton, and will eventually build her transcendent nation in Rim Billiton."
This was a rumor Angelina heard in a slum neighborhood in Deep Iron Works. She failed to track down the whereabouts of the speaker, but this remark has always weighed heavily on her mind.

Setting aside the incident at Red Sand Town, Angelina herself is also an Infected. She was in very bad shape when she first arrived at Rhodes Island, and to this day, her own Oripathy is not entirely devoid of signs of progression, while one of the friends she made this time, Jacinta, is an even more advanced Oripathy patient... We indeed worry that these factors combined might have a negative impact on Angelina's psychological state.
Unexpectedly, Angelina answered us this way:
"I won't say things like 'there's always a way.' Some things simply have no way out. We can only watch them happen, trying our best to delay and remedy them, and even when doing our best, we often still don't get the ending we want.
"But no matter what, I will never lose hope. The hope the Doctor initially brought me... indeed had impractical elements to it, but even a false hope is precious to me. In fact, without that bit of hope, it would be impossible for me to be standing here in front of everyone like this today.
"What's more, even if hope isn't built on a completely solid foundation, the feelings contained within it are entirely genuine."

handbook.char_1015_aglna2.story.7.text.text:
...And just like that, another jar is filled to the brim with paper stars.
Actually, I couldn't even tell you anymore why these stars were folded in the first place. It has simply become a habit: when I delivered a letter, when I accomplished something, when I failed to accomplish something, when I said something that I felt a bit proud of upon reflection, when there was something I couldn't bring myself to say...
Yet if it's just folding paper, if it's just hiding one's feelings inside paper-folded stars... then some things will never be known by anyone else. Stars do not speak. Stars are silent eyes. They know, but they never tell. No one knows what the stars are thinking.
And as for me... I know it is impossible for me to sparkle in the sky forever like the twinkling stars. Martina said that the emotions hidden in one's heart will eventually change, but for me, perhaps at some moment before those emotions have even changed, I will have already transformed into a shooting star flashing across the edge of the sky. Therefore, I should boldly speak out, express my longing for my Mom and Dad, my attachment to Rhodes Island, my care for my friends, and speak the words hidden deep in the bottom of my heart... to the important people, leaving behind no further regrets.
Well, Angelina's paper stars are only this many. If there are still things you are too shy to say for the moment... just use this, the paper-folded Perro beast companion Mom first taught me, the "little fox."
It is not a star; it doesn't have to spend the rest of its life waiting for a companion star. It will proactively find the person it wishes to accompany, stay by that person's side, lean on that person, and occasionally let that person lean on it.
It is not merely about embraces and dances, but also about backing each other up in times of danger, and providing support for each other's shoulders when strength fails.

handbook.char_1015_aglna2.story.8.text.text:
[Voice Record]
It's fine. I just finished training, the timing is just right, not early at all.
Uh... no. I don't have anything urgent to find you for. Is this kind of inappropriate? If you have more important things to attend to—
Ngh—hm, alright! I'm glad the Doctor could carve out time specifically for me.
Actually, it's like this. Earlier I helped Ms. Haze deliver a letter that was very important to her, so she gave me a reading... A very serious divination, which took a heavy toll on her.
She saw my figure in the crystal ball, and she said it should be the future me... But that's not really the point. The point is, I was caught in the middle of a war, seemingly defending a defense line.
No matter how much I participate in Rhodes Island's field missions, I am still a messenger. If a war reaches the point where even a messenger is indispensable, what on earth will Rhodes Island, or even this land... become?
...Saying I'm not scared would be a lie. I am very afraid of a future like that, and even though Ms. Haze saw some different sights later on, that blurry battlefield still appears in my dreams, which is why I came to find you.
Me in the crystal ball? Hm... Ms. Haze said my figure in the crystal ball was completely fearless... If the me of that time can truly pull that off, that would be wonderful.
But... if we really have to face a war, I hope I can still leap for joy over a meal filled with genuine care, feel comforted by a letter reporting my safety, relax my brow slightly over a meticulously blended fragrance... and leave at least a fleeting glance of time for a freshly blooming flower.
You don't know if you can make this wish of mine come true, but you will work hard for it?
I'm very happy, though... I might... have a request that's a bit hard on you.
This... could this also become your wish?
...Thank you, Doctor.
Just like you, I will... give it my all for this wish.

handbook.char_1048_orchd2.story.4.text.text:
The magazine "Orchid" is practically a household name on Rhodes Island today. Spearheaded by Ms. Orchid and named after her own Operator codename, this fashion magazine boasts a level of detail and a professional perspective that never fails to amaze. Today, our editor is fortunate enough to interview the founder of the magazine, Ms. Orchid.
Editor: Excuse me, Ms. Orchid, what was the inspiration behind founding this magazine?
Orchid: Ever since joining Rhodes Island, one of the things I've constantly been doing is helping the Infected conceal the crystals on their bodies through fashion and trends. The number of operators and patients who came to me for this... really was quite a lot. All I can say is, everyone is human, and everyone has the right to pursue fashion; I think that's a good thing. However, too many people were coming in, so I figured, rather than having them come one by one, I might as well teach everyone some methods all at once.
Editor: So you founded this magazine?
Orchid: No. To be honest, the HR department's work is busy to death. Even though I had tossed that idea around in my head, I never actually thought about making it a reality.
Editor: Eh? Then—
Orchid: There was a period when Beagle and Spot found me too annoying and wanted to find something for me to do, so they went behind my back and applied for the production of the magazine, even putting together a proper sample issue to give me for my birthday. I was actually quite touched back then, but thinking about it now, it was utterly stupid. However, since the work was already done and I felt the opportunity was rare, I took it over and kept running it.
Editor: Then what about these names written on the masthead—
Graphic Design: Spot
Editing and Proofreading: Midnight
Models: Spot, Midnight, Popukar, Beagle...
Special Contributor: Beagle
Could it be—
Orchid: Heh, they made up their minds that I would take over, did they really think they could run away?
Editor: I-I see. However, while magazines, training classes, and interest corners founded by operators based on their own interests are numerous on board, the stability of their content output and activity frequency is mostly affected by the busyness of the operators' own missions and their duration of stay on the landship. As a monthly magazine, "Orchid" has not missed a single month of publication since its inception. In other words, although the beginning might not have been so wonderful, the process and outcome are good, right?
Orchid: Right, Spot?
Spot: Just kill me, don't make me do graphic design anymore, I just want to read manga.
Orchid: What about Midnight?
Midnight: Spare me, Ms. Orchid, the two words "clothing" are starting to make me completely break down.
Orchid: Beagle?
Beagle: I never wrote this many words even when I was in school!
Orchid: And Popukar?
Popukar: I love being a model for Big Sis Orchid!
Orchid: Spot honed his drawing skills, Midnight had less time to go around harassing others, Beagle had time to study, Popukar got new clothes to wear, and I could also do something I've always been interested in. It's really quite nice, isn't it?
Editor: ...Ahaha, let's talk about the matter of gathering material!

handbook.char_1048_orchd2.story.5.text.text:
After finishing her report on her bizarre journey, Suzuran secretly submitted an application to find out why Dr. Kal'tsit had brought Popukar back to Rhodes Island in the first place.
After learning the full picture of the Phantom Realm incident, the Doctor and Amiya agreed that this was necessary. In the past, everyone only knew that Popukar's eyes were special, but having unusual eyes was not rare on Rhodes Island. However, Suzuran's experience seemed to prove that Popukar's eyes and background were far from simple.
This wasn't because Suzuran didn't trust Rhodes Island and Dr. Kal'tsit—quite the contrary. After all, it was simply impossible for Dr. Kal'tsit not to know about Popukar's background. Why, then, had she kept it a secret? That question became a lingering doubt in Suzuran's heart.
At the meeting called for this matter, Dr. Kal'tsit first expressed her apologies to Suzuran. Because Suzuran and Conangu's ordeal exceeded her imagination, she was unable to clearly explain to Suzuran the connection between Popukar and the Treasure Witch, and she needed time to sort out the specifics.
However, Dr. Kal'tsit gave a definitive reply regarding the matter Suzuran was truly worried about. From the very beginning, Dr. Kal'tsit had no other intention in assigning Popukar to Reserve Team A6 than hoping Suzuran would take care of her, and no other environment could possibly make Popukar feel more at ease now. For the sake of Popukar's mental stability, Dr. Kal'tsit also hoped that Team A6 could stay closely connected.
"Popukar is just a good kid growing up thriving on Rhodes Island, and that will never change no matter what."
Suzuran accepted this reply.
When it came down to it, she didn't care what secrets were buried within Popukar. It might be important, but not that important to her. Just like her expectations for herself and everyone around her, she only hoped Popukar could live a happy life.
After the meeting ended, she already had an idea in mind—she had already told the others of A6 about her experience in the Phantom Realm once, but she planned to tell it again. This time, she would make sure to focus on the overly eccentric blacksmith, the overly serious general, and that overly resilient princess.

handbook.char_1048_orchd2.story.6.text.text:
Suzuran had a very good relationship with her family.
In this regard, she could be said to be an anomaly in A6. After all, Popukar was picked up by Dr. Kal'tsit, Yato and Spot had almost completely severed ties with their families, and as for Conangu, being an orphan, she didn't even know what her parents were called.
The other members of A6 did not shy away from talking about Suzuran's family. They all knew that Suzuran's parents cared deeply about their daughter's health and didn't distance themselves just because she contracted Oripathy, and Suzuran would regularly write letters to contact her parents and report on her recent status. Regarding this, the members of A6 all considered it a good thing.
Suzuran admitted that she was lucky enough in this regard. Her parents had never restricted her choices regarding work and the future, and after she accidentally contracted Oripathy, they also supported her choice to go to Rhodes Island, always telling her that she could come home whenever she wanted and they were willing to give up many things for her.
Her parents were always concerned about her, always asking if she had any plans to return—which was only natural. In the eyes of many, no matter how famous a pharmaceutical enterprise Rhodes Island was, as long as it was related to infected individuals, the future was always precarious. In the eyes of Suzuran's family, living on Rhodes Island was ultimately not such a good choice—
"...Your mother and I have discussed it. We can sell the house and move to a more remote place to live together. Your mother and I can take care of you, so you don't have to worry about anything... We believe Rhodes Island is a good company, but what is more blissful than a family reunion?"
Her father had said this in a letter, and at that time, she found herself unable to give a reply.
How should she answer? Tell her parents that she was actually doing fairly well working here, and had made a group of friends who were eccentric in personality but not bad at heart?
So what? That didn't seem to conflict with going home. No job could be done for a lifetime, and no friends would stay together forever, but family was different; family was connected by blood. Moreover, her family loved her so much, and she loved her parents as well.
She didn't have any grand ambitions. She felt Rhodes Island's ideals were great and was willing to do her part for the Infected within her power—or rather, before she knew it, she had already invested several years of her life into this cause. She had also understood the thoughts of Elite Operators, but she felt she couldn't do what they did.
It seemed like staying as she was for now was fine. When her condition worsened further to the point where she couldn't work, or for some other reason, she would leave this place, return to her parents, and then calmly await the arrival of death.
For an Infected, this was already a sufficiently happy life.
She had imagined such a thing, but she had never been able to pick up her pen to reply to her parents. Something was holding her back, and she couldn't explain what it was, so she was always vague and avoided the subject.
And this wasn't the first time.

handbook.char_1048_orchd2.story.7.text.text:
In the days when she hadn't yet contracted Oripathy and was still working as a magazine editor, her parents would also ask her if this was her ideal job. She hadn't given an answer then either.
She liked fashion and she liked tailoring, but should she pursue this career as her lifelong goal? She felt she couldn't make a conclusion. She couldn't completely stop thinking about the choices facing her, so she always thought a lot. This made it seem to others that she was always prepared for the future, but only she knew that she was merely lucky enough to have the power of choice in certain matters.
Making a choice that determined one's entire life was simply too difficult; after all, a person's life was too long—she used to think that way in the past, but she couldn't use that to demand her parents not discuss the issue either. Later on, her parents even stopped mentioning such discussions in their home letters because they knew it would cause her inner turmoil. When it came down to it, she knew this was an ultimate question that even she herself wanted to find the answer to—
What did she actually want to do with her life?
And before she could find an answer, she contracted Oripathy. Coming to Rhodes Island for treatment, becoming an Operator, serving as the leader of A6, and in the blink of an eye, several years had passed.
Regarding the answer to this ultimate question, she still had no clue. Not only that, but the pain brought by Oripathy constantly reminded her that her life was no longer as long as she once imagined.
It was simply hopeless. After returning from Sargon, facing yet another home letter, she thought this.
Even more despairing was her realization that now, whenever she thought "a person's life is too long," she would instinctively add a line in Spot's tone—"Well, at least now that you've got Oripathy, it's not that long anymore."
forget about making progress, she felt she had already been assimilated by this bunch... Amidst Popukar's astonished gaze, she slumped onto the desk in dismay.
Come to think of it, over these past few years, she really didn't seem to have made any progress at all.
She remembered Penny and Jerry, and that wedding dress that still appeared in her dreams to this day. She recalled that night a thousand times, yet still couldn't think of a better way to handle it.
She remembered what Conangu said at the very end when hunting the Zinogre. Yes, she always exhorted those around her that life should have an answer, but in truth, she had no answer for it herself.
She was always like this, saying one thing while meaning another, demanding things from others that she might not even be able to do herself.
Sometimes she quite hated herself like this.
Even after enduring such a hard journey through the Phantom Realm, the only things she could call gains besides this set of equipment and some memories were simply becoming a little bit more honest with herself.
However, when she turned her attention back to how to reply to her parents' letter, she was somewhat surprised to find that this time, aside from routine updates on her current status and warm regards, she had some other things she wanted to write.
"...I've introduced my teammates to you many times, but everyone hasn't had much of a chance to meet and chat. I was thinking recently, perhaps the next time I go on a field assignment in Columbia, I can bring them to meet you."
She wrote this passage almost as a matter of course.
This was, of course, not an answer.
It was just that sometimes, being a little more honest with oneself meant letting go of certain obsessions. Perhaps some jobs could be done for a lifetime, perhaps some friends could be gotten along with for a lifetime, and perhaps these things were not in conflict.
She decided to give it a try.

handbook.char_1048_orchd2.story.8.text.text:
Suzuran appeared at the training grounds much more often than before.
This didn't attract as much attention as Conangu's transformation; after all, Suzuran had always been the type to conscientiously complete her training. Now, in the eyes of others, she merely seemed a bit more proactive than usual.
However, Dobermann, acting as her instructor, noticed some subtle changes.
In the past, Suzuran completed her training merely to meet the metrics required of an Operator, lacking any desire to improve her own combat capabilities beyond that baseline. But returning from Sargon, wearing a new set of equipment, and even changing her tactical positioning, Suzuran had indeed made some changes in this regard.
Yet Dobermann also knew that this couldn't simply be summarized as Suzuran developing the desire to become stronger, or having some new thoughts about combat. One only needed to stand beside Suzuran and observe her state during training to know this.
She was more like she was searching for something within combat.
Before a certain training session, Dobermann and Suzuran chatted about this topic.
"...Stand firm, nock the arrow, aim, draw the bow, release. The steps of archery are as simple and understandable as designing a garment." Facing Dobermann, an instructor and friend she had dealt with for years, Suzuran thought about the question seriously.
"So you feel it shares some commonalities with your hobby?"
"No." Suzuran shook her head. "Designing garments requires thinking about many things; it requires creativity. While archery... to me, what's important is that during archery, I can just focus on aiming at the target without having to think about anything else."
Suzuran paused, seemingly expending some effort before finally speaking her next sentence: "I can control it. Yes, I should say, it's something I can completely control."
"Control?" Dobermann was somewhat surprised to hear such a word come from Suzuran's mouth.
"Yes. I've heard before that through small tasks like folding clothes and cleaning, people can accumulate a sense of control over their lives bit by bit, ultimately gaining the confidence to face life. I didn't believe these things before, but..." Suzuran picked up the bow in her hand as she spoke, stood firm, nocked the arrow, aimed, drew the bow, and released, the arrow hitting dead center in the target, "in the process of archery, I really do feel like I can control myself just a little bit."
"What surprises me is that you also need to use this method to anchor yourself."
"Honestly, I'm surprised myself." Suzuran smiled somewhat helplessly. "Still, how should I put it? I've never been someone with a lot of confidence in anything, and I don't know if this feeling actually works. It's just that whenever I feel upset now, I want to practice archery."
With that, Suzuran picked up her bow and arrows and walked toward the training ground. Watching her, Dobermann was both gladdened that she had found a new interest and astonished at her lack of self-awareness in a certain area.
"Does she not realize that simply standing firm, nocking the arrow, aiming, drawing the bow, and releasing to hit the target isn't actually something everyone can do?"

handbook.char_1049_catap2.story.2.text.text:
Reserve Team A6 member. Per her own request, her position was changed to Guard Operator, and she has displayed a very strong talent for close-quarters combat and the use of heavy melee weapons. Outside of Team A6's daily missions, she also frequently participates in various field missions requiring trips to hazardous areas under her own name.
Everyone says that Conangu, who used to love slacking off and being slick, has completely changed. To such evaluations, she is noncommittal.

handbook.char_1049_catap2.story.3.text.text:
Imaging tests reveal blurred organ outlines with abnormal shadows visible in the thoracic cavity. Originium granule detection in circulatory system is abnormal, confirming signs of Oripathy infection. At this stage, the subject is confirmed to be infected with Oripathy.

[Cell-Originium Fusion Rate] 5%
Operator Conangu exhibits obvious symptoms of infection.

[Blood Originium Crystal Density] 0.33u/L
Due to frequent forays into high-risk environments and participation in high-intensity combat, Operator Conangu's condition carries a risk of worsening.

handbook.char_1049_catap2.story.4.text.text:
Regarding the mission report of the trip to the Phantom Realm, Suzuran and Conangu each submitted a version. Suzuran's version was meticulous as always, allowing one to clearly understand the ins and outs of the matter, while Conangu's left people unsure whether to laugh or cry—
She submitted a report that seemed extremely detailed to her, but the contents were solely related to hunting.
Yes, just looking at Conangu's mission report, you would never know what she and Suzuran had encountered in the Phantom Realm, but after reading it, you would definitely know what kind of environment surrounded the Phantom Realm, what monsters inhabited it, and whether those monsters were edible.
Even Suzuran was astonished upon reading it, wondering when on earth Conangu had gathered such intelligence. Conangu, on the other hand, proudly listed them to Suzuran one by one: what dishes eaten in the Phantom Realm actually had ingredients sourced from which monsters, what meat eaten by the campfire on a certain occasion came from which monster, and so on, stating that it was simply because Suzuran was worried sick all day and hadn't cared about such things at all.
I must say, Conangu's material was undoubtedly a zero as a mission report, but as a local gazetteer, it could be said to be a hundred.
Moreover, the adventure of the two was simply too bizarre. No matter how meticulously Suzuran wrote, it would inevitably arouse doubt, and Conangu's report successfully dispelled these doubts—anyone with good eloquence could make up a story, but concocting a complete ecosystem was truly something ordinary people could never accomplish.

handbook.char_1049_catap2.story.6.text.text:
In the job transfer evaluation report for Conangu submitted to the Doctor, Dobermann specifically mentioned Conangu's attitude toward combat, as follows:
I have met many warriors who love combat itself, and there are quite a few such people on Rhodes Island. Their general attitude toward combat is—"I hope to prove through combat that I am growing stronger, I am fighting against myself, and I want to constantly surpass myself." Combat to them is a test.
At first, when I heard others mention Conangu's situation, I thought her personality had changed and even found it a bit strange, feeling it wasn't like her.
After testing her, I understood immediately. Her attitude... I have seen it in certain people before. What these people pursue is not simply becoming stronger, but the thrilling sensation of a razor-thin margin between life and death. Conangu is the same. She has no thoughts of challenging her own limits or having a dialogue with herself; she simply feels that fighting huge monsters is thrilling enough to relieve the boredom in her heart.
Put this way, I can conversely understand why she would undergo such a transformation.
The commonality between these two types of people is that they can both grow stronger very quickly, while the difference is that people like Conangu tend to have very short lives.
A Felyne named Masamune seems to appreciate this Hunter-like trait of hers, which I can understand. In the context of nature, this is indeed unproblematic—failing constantly, challenging constantly, growing stronger constantly, they themselves become part of the law of the jungle.
Of course, I can also understand your worry, Doctor. For people of this sort, all tempering is merely for the pursuit of more intense thrills, and the consequence of infinitely pursuing such thrills is bound to be destructive.
However, I feel you needn't worry too much.
Compared to her "own kind," Conangu has some differences.
If I were to summarize it, I would say it is—impurity. Conangu can never manage to throw herself entirely into the hunt.
And the reason is obvious, isn't it?

handbook.char_1049_catap2.story.7.text.text:
Conangu quickly made a name for herself in some explorer and hunter circles, and many professional teams extended olive branches to her, all of which she rejected.
She had considered this issue because Sister Suzuran would always earnestly tell everyone in Team A6 not to just focus on the present, but to think more about the future.
Clearly, this was the question Sister Suzuran wanted her to think about.
Occasionally—most of the time when she was extremely bored—she would also ask herself: What do you want to do in the future?
Even more occasionally, in order to respond to Sister Suzuran's expectant gaze, she would try very hard to come up with an answer, but she found she truly couldn't.
She seemed destined never to become someone who prepared for the future like Sister Suzuran.
Yet she didn't feel she was someone who enjoyed the present moment either, after all, such people weren't as lazy as she was.
She shirked training, treated missions perfunctorily, and besides Team A6, had no desire to maintain interpersonal relationships.
Sister Suzuran always criticized her for muddle-headedness, and she herself felt she was muddle-headed, but actually, she knew she just didn't understand the meaning of those things.
Vaguely, she felt she was waiting—waiting for something that could truly make her invest her energy to appear.
She told this conclusion to Sister Suzuran, and Sister Suzuran would say: "If you don't try, you'll never find what suits you."
Now, she felt she seemed to have found it. She liked hunting, so finding a team dedicated to hunting seemed like a better choice. She dared say Sister Suzuran would definitely support this idea—at least on the surface.
But she wasn't as awkward as Sister Suzuran. Sister Suzuran wouldn't admit she liked Team A6, but she was different.
She never denied that she liked everyone in Team A6, liked their personalities, liked that unique space that only came into being when they were together.
Ask her to give this up? Then she'd rather give up hunting.
Yes, so what she was worried about wasn't whether she should leave Team A6 for her own pursuits, but how she was going to persuade the rest of Team A6 to join her hunting enterprise—couldn't persuade them? Then she'd just drag them along!
She already had some ideas. She could trick—oh, I mean, convince Spot to draw a hunting manga together, with her writing the script and Spot doing the art, and then use the engaging plot to hook Popukar and make her fall in love with hunting too. Yatoh was a bit troublesome... right, she had collected so many business cards, it wouldn't hurt to have him do some actual work. As for Sister Suzuran, ah, if everyone else came, Sister Suzuran would definitely come too!
That's right, it's settled!
She thought with self-satisfaction, one day, she was going to hunt the fiercest beasts on the land! By then, Team A6 would definitely be the strongest team on this land too! Probably!

handbook.char_1049_catap2.story.8.text.text:
The weapon usage guide brought by Masamune details the moves of various hunting weapons. Today, the blank sections of the Charge Blade guide have been completely filled with Popuko's notes.
Of course, calling them notes would be a stretch, as most of it isn't particularly serious content.
For instance, next to "Morph Slash", she drew numerous vertical lines to keep track of how many times she failed to transform in time and crashed into a wall.
And right above "Counter Peak Performance", she wrote two large lines of text—"Don't forget to check the Wirebug's status when using this! It can only block one attack! Don't rely on it too much!"—along with a doodle of herself being sent flying by a monster because she got too cocky.
The notes next to "Axe Hopper" are even more speechless. While there are some combat tips concerning hitzones, most of it consists of her researching what posture looks the coolest when unleashing her aerial Super Elemental Discharge, and it seems she didn't come to a conclusion until the very end.
However, right next to "Condensed Spinning Slash", she earnestly jotted down some of her own thoughts—
Focusing one's spirit into a single instant, defending against the opponent's strongest blow, and then counterattacking with my strongest Super Elemental Discharge—that grand and dynamic feeling is the true essence of the Charge Blade.
Yet this move is also quite fascinating, as it practically changes the style of the Charge Blade—instead of relying on split-second guards and powerful moves, it focuses on situational awareness, looking for openings while dodging enemy attacks. Plus, the handling feels just like Popuko's chainsaw. It's a pity we couldn't use it back in the Mirage Realm.
I still prefer the former, but Condensed Spinning Slash has its own fun, haha. And Axe Hopper is a blast too! The Charge Blade is truly even more interesting than I initially imagined!

handbook.char_4215_buddy.story.2.text.text:
Composed of the Palico Masamune and the Palamute Yoshitsune, the Rhodes Island Covert Team takes its name from their affiliation back in their hometown of Kamura Village—the "Buddy Recon Team". Having received professional training in intelligence investigation and material collection, and honed over a long period in the Mirage Realm, Masamune and Yoshitsune immediately played vital roles in various missions upon joining Rhodes Island. While they hope to find a way back home, they are also quite keen on adventuring across Terra, allowing them to adapt rather well to life here.
Lively and friendly, Masamune quickly became a star among the operators—many apply to go on missions with him just to catch a glimpse of the talkative, adorable "cloud beast". Meanwhile, the normally aloof Yoshitsune has also hit it off with numerous combat-enthusiast operators.

handbook.char_4215_buddy.story.3.text.text:
Imaging tests reveal clear organ outlines in both operators with no abnormal shadows. Originium particle detection in the circulatory system shows no abnormalities, with no signs of Oripathy infection. At this stage, they can be confirmed as uninfected.

[Cell-Originium Fusion Rate] 0%
Neither Masamune nor Yoshitsune shows any signs of Originium infection.

[Blood Originium Crystal Density] Undefined
Per Medical Department resolution, relevant data will not be made public.

handbook.char_4215_buddy.story.4.text.text:
When discussing the concept of "hunters" with members of Team A6, Masamune dropped his usual liveliness and turned rather serious, while Yoshitsune, dozing nearby, pricked up his ears.
In their homeland, a hunter's duty is to protect the ecosystem while hunting monsters. Consequently, every hunter is a pioneer exploring the unknown; for instance, the "Flame of Kamura" was the great hero who resolved Kamura Village's crisis—the Rampage.
"An outstanding hunter shares one trait—the indomitable spirit of challenge, meow!"
No matter how tricky the enemy, no matter how many times they fail, a true hunter will continually issue challenges until victory is secured or they fall. In Masamune's words, a "hunter" is not merely a profession, but a symbol of spirit.
"Sounds like the furthest thing from our little squad," Spot couldn't help chiming in.
"I think so too. I'm nothing that great; I just do it because it's fun," Popuko echoed. The spirit of challenge? She certainly didn't think her reasons for picking up the Charge Blade were that noble.
Yet Masamune shook his head.
"If it were before, I might have thought so too, meow. But things are different now. Whether it's the people of the Mirage Realm or Rhodes Island, their targets and reasons for fighting might differ from hunters, meow! Everyone here possesses the spirit of challenge, meow!"

handbook.char_4217_makoto.story.2.text.text:
Makoto Yuki was registered as a relative of a Laterano citizen at the Atrium Notary Office in March 1102. In accordance with Article 34 of the Appendix to the Laterano Civil Rights Charter, he was admitted to St. Marso Comprehensive School.
Teacher's Comments: Student Makoto Yuki is calm in his dealings, unites well with his peers, respects his teachers, and actively participates in social practical activities, earning unanimous praise in volunteer practice. We hope he maintains this perseverance, continues to strive, and reaches even greater heights.

handbook.char_4217_makoto.story.4.text.text:
Makoto Yuki is known for his low-profile and reticent demeanor, which once led to concerns over whether he could smoothly integrate into Laterano's campus life. However, his subsequent performance proved those worries entirely unfounded.
On the day of the school anniversary, Aigis approached Amiya for help, stating she could not find Makoto. For reasons of her own, Amiya was also searching for her homeroom teacher at the time, so the two teamed up for the anniversary search party. The celebratory events organized by various classes varied greatly in nature—some risky enough to turn the anniversary into a prank convention of swapping hostages—and Aigis seemed worried that Makoto might get into trouble. Amiya comforted her, explaining that to prevent such situations, the school had strongly encouraged celebrations to return to tradition this year, meaning the worst danger Makoto faced was likely blood sugar fluctuations from consuming excess carbohydrates at the endless rows of sweet stalls.
Just as Amiya predicted, the two found Makoto in the confectionery street: almost every sweet stall reported that Makoto had been helping out there just moments ago. According to them, Makoto first helped churn milk base at the ice cream stall, then went to the canelé stall to mix batter, followed by filling puffs at the cream puff stall, and his last recorded sighting was squeezing chestnut puree at the Mont Blanc stall. Finally, Aigis and Amiya found Makoto at the end of the street, waiting in a long line at the creperie, where he was making a "Holy Spirit Ascending Cumulonimbus Crepe," hyped for having a crepe filling stacked as high as a May cumulonimbus cloud. The student running the stall begged Aigis not to take Makoto away: "I know Makoto isn't in our class, but customers have waited so long in line for his special crepe..."
"Ah, is the crepe chef going off shift?" asked a blue-haired Sankta waiting in line, turning to her red-haired Liberi companion. "Fiammetta, your luck is the worst."
"What does that have to do with me?" the Liberi replied dismissively, before turning back to ask, "Excuse me, we've been waiting for a long time, can you really not make two more... or even just one?"
The student running the stall looked troubled as they glanced at Aigis and Makoto.
"If Makoto cannot leave, then I shall remain here to keep Makoto company," Aigis nodded.
"Aigis, aren't you coming with me to look for the teacher?" Amiya asked, somewhat troubled. "I was hoping that if you could help, searching together..."
"Aigis, go help Amiya find Doctor," Makoto said calmly as he spread crepe batter. "You can come back and look for me afterward. I'll wait for you."
"Doesn't Makoto need to go to other stalls? By the way, why did you help out at so many..." Amiya asked curiously.
"I'll be staying here afterward. My friends asked me to," Makoto replied while arranging fruit.
"Oh~ I think I saw you at the cream puff and Mont Blanc stalls earlier," said the blue-haired Sankta. "You have that many friends?"
"Not really." Makoto drizzled five times the amount of maple syrup onto the crepe and handed it to the long-waiting customer.
Later, all the transfer students learned about what happened on the anniversary, and it is said they discussed it in the dormitories—not discussing why Makoto was helping everywhere, as they were already used to that, but rather discussing when Makoto had learned how to make so many kinds of desserts. However, the transfer students failed to reach a consensus. The S.E.E.S. leader's learning capability truly seemed to be an enigma.

handbook.char_4217_makoto.story.5.text.text:
It is said that a sports club once extended an invitation to Makoto, but perhaps because the school's athletic clubs mostly focused on gun-martial arts or similar disciplines, Makoto did not join any of them. When it came to extracurricular activities, he had other choices.
One day after school, Makoto asked Yukari if she knew of any nearby places to work part-time. Yukari looked a bit surprised. "The school welfare is pretty good, there doesn't seem to be any need for a part-time job... Is there something you want to buy?"
Makoto nodded without offering a detailed explanation. Their conversation was overheard by Ambriel passing by; her eyes rolled, and she cheerfully sidled up, asking if Makoto had any free time today. Ambriel often took up part-time jobs to buy various trendy goods or accepted strange commissions from classmates, something the students had heard plenty about.
Makoto accepted Ambriel's proposal, and Ambriel led him and Yukari to—the most popular arcade in the St. Marceau District. She bypassed fifty bizarre shooting games and dragged the two to a side-scrolling platformer arcade cabinet.
"This job—well, actually, it's a commission from your classmate Randolph. He wants the event bonus item for this game, which requires clearing all six major maps within the time limit to redeem, including the two-player mode." Ambriel bit on a lollipop and spread her hands. "As you can see, very few people play this. Team up with me, commission fee split fifty-fifty. How about it?"
Makoto stared at the game screen in deep thought, and finally nodded to Ambriel. Seeing that the two of them would likely need some time to get used to it, Yukari decided to try out a few of the fifty shooting games—surely video games didn't require Arts to fire a weapon.
Before she could even try a few shots, Yukari heard Ambriel's excited shouting: "You're pretty good, huh?! Alright, keep going, keep going!" By the time Yukari had finished playing and returned to the side-scrolling cabinet, she happened to see Makoto and Ambriel claiming the clear reward trophy for the final map.
"So what is it that Makoto actually wants to buy?" Yukari asked on the way back to the dormitory.
"Um... book covers, glass flower vases, and things like that," Makoto replied. "I feel like Doctor and the president would like those kinds of gifts. I want to give them out before leaving."
"Ah..."
"I also want to try other part-time jobs."
"Is the money still not enough?"
"I still want to see more of what happens in this city. Since I'm here."
Yukari smiled. "So that's why you wanted to work part-time?"
Makoto didn't answer; the dormitory was already in sight. Pushing open the door, the lounge felt both familiar and unfamiliar, and he heard a voice say, "Welcome back."

handbook.char_4217_makoto.story.6.text.text:
Makoto came to my office one afternoon, leaving behind two gift boxes—one for me and one for the president, he said. With our parting soon approaching, he wanted to thank us for taking care of them during this time. Amiya looked a bit dejected; she had always been reluctant to dwell on the thought that "Makoto and the others will be leaving soon." Still, she quickly perked up, saying she would accept the gifts as birthday presents.
Learning that Amiya's birthday was in winter, Makoto wished her an early happy birthday. We chatted about Amiya's past birthdays and touched upon the time she was first adopted. Makoto didn't seem surprised, nodding to note that Laterano people seemed fond of adopting children. I explained that Amiya was not adopted from the Wordsmith Residence. Makoto seemed somewhat curious about the topic, so I chatted with him a bit more. Laterano's social environment is somewhat unique; a considerable proportion of residents never form families in their lives, and as a result, many Laterano children (especially Sankta) are sent to the Wordsmith Residence for upbringing from birth—this is Laterano's public childcare institution. Some children grow up in the Wordsmith Residence until adulthood, while others are adopted. Due to the existence of Resonance and Laterano's social system, Laterano people believe every child is a child of God, whether they grow up in the Wordsmith Residence or within a family. Of course, no one can say for sure whether this will change in the future.
After listening to this introduction, Makoto seemed to be deep in thought. Amiya also seemed a bit curious about Makoto's upbringing; she glanced at me first, and though I understood her thoughts, I still shook my head.
I followed up by asking Makoto if he would like to visit the Wordsmith Residence. He hesitated for a moment, but agreed. At the Wordsmith Residence, we also ran into a former student, Spuria, who now works in the Sixth Department and happened to be visiting the friars that day. We accompanied the children to play for a while and helped the friars with some chores. When we left, the sun was setting. Noticing Makoto was a foreigner, Spuria gave him a wink before parting, saying, "Isn't a place like this in Laterano interesting?" Makoto nodded. "Yeah, the children all seem happy."
On the way back to the dormitory with Makoto, he shared some amusing anecdotes about himself and his friends in the Moonlight Dormitory at Gekkoukan High School. Although fighting the Shadows was hard work, in their daily lives, these children lived ordinary and simple student lives as well. Makoto's steady voice seemed to convey the contentment in his heart.
At the dormitory entrance, he said to us, "Doctor, Amiya, thank you for showing me around today." The newly risen moon cast a slightly ethereal glow upon his figure.
"Don't mention it, Makoto..." Amiya said to him. She trailed off, but finally spoke up: "I've always felt... there are family members bestowed by the heavens, and there are family members you choose for yourself. The path to happiness isn't predestined... I chose the teacher as my family, and that is my own happiness."
Makoto smiled softly. "Yeah, I think so too."

handbook.char_4217_makoto.story.7.text.text:
Makoto said that ever since coming to Laterano, he hasn't dreamed once. He asked me if this was because coming to Laterano itself was a dream. People only stop dreaming once inside a dream.
I told him, if I were a person in your dream, how do you think I would answer?
Afterward, I took Makoto for a walk around the city of Laterano. Some places he might have visited, while others I guessed he hadn't. I showed him the shopping street where Amiya and I usually buy things, took him to my favorite bookstore, listened to people play the violin in the plaza before the Papal Palace, walked past the hospital where Kal'tsit works, overlooked the apple blossoms downstairs from the school rooftop, passed by the now officially opened mortuary, and finally reached the edge of the mobile city.
Looking at the low hills in the distance, it makes the mobile city's progress feel unhurried. I asked Makoto if he still thought this felt like a dream. He was silent for a moment, then said not anymore, as he had felt so much within this city. This place is good.
Just a small coincidence, I said. There are still many corners of this land; if their journey were to pass through those places, it would likely be much harder.
"Have you been to all those places?" he asked me. I replied that I had been to some, while many others I had yet to set foot in.
"Will you go in the future, Doctor?" Makoto asked next.
I said I would.
Makoto smiled gently. "This world outside Laterano... no, 'this land' still seems vast. If I have the chance to see it, that would be great. Maybe I could even help the Doctor out."
I nodded. The days of parting were drawing near, but why bring it up at this moment? The mobile city was still moving forward, night had yet to fall, and when speaking of the future, we could always hope this journey would stretch onward into the distance.

handbook.char_4217_makoto.story.8.text.text:
Makoto Yuki is undoubtedly the core of this group called the Special Extracurricular Execution Squad (S.E.E.S.), referred to by other members as the "Leader." Based on my observations of their combat, although these transfer students all possess the ability to summon "Personas," Makoto Yuki appears to be the only one among them capable of summoning multiple "Personas." Additionally, Aigis's focus on him is worth investigating—it goes beyond ordinary friendship or trust (considering Aigis's incomplete self-awareness), yet neither Makoto nor Aigis herself can clearly explain this matter at present. He seems to harbor a strong will, firmly desiring a return to his original world, and drives the others to unswervingly seek a path back. He is indeed their leader, for he is constantly considering these companions.
Makoto sometimes reminds me of Amiya; they are somewhat similar, holding fast to a powerful will and resolutely choosing kindness. They might protect many people, or even save the fate of the world, but what a heavy burden this is, and what does it mean for them personally? It's just... even with worry, I understand that such children will ultimately walk the path few tread, bearing the choices they have settled on, not for themselves, but for more people.

Teacher's Comments: Student Aigis is intelligent, studious, rigorous, and highly responsible, with strict self-discipline. She has achieved commendable results in gun-martial arts series courses. It is hoped she will open up her heart more, try participating in group activities, and enjoy a wonderful campus life alongside her academic progress.
