handbook.char_4218_aigis.story.4.text.text:
Following her enrollment, student Aigis garnered considerable attention from classmates due to her performance in gun-martial arts courses. Aigis is not a Sankta, yet she wields and skillfully operates multiple weapons resembling firearms. At the conclusion of a certain gun-martial arts class, the adjacent class's Sesa asked whether she was using the rumored replica firearms developed in Columbia, and whether her special way of holding them was related to that. Aigis answered these questions with utmost seriousness; it was not difficult to see that neither the speaker nor the listener understood what the other was talking about.
Dr. {@nickname}, passing by, silently listened for five minutes to the two students' cross-purposed discussion before taking over the topic. They segued from Columbian security company replica firearms to experimental weapons that briefly appeared in Sargon, then discussed the similarities and differences between Iberia-style hand cannons and Laterano-style launchers, and even mentioned research once attempted by Closure of the engineering club. Sesa listened with rapt attention, entirely forgetting the question he had originally posed to Aigis. Aigis similarly listened intently to Dr.{@nickname}'s impromptu lecture on gun-martial equipment development, a gleam flashing in her eyes from time to time.
After the lecture concluded, Aigis followed Dr.{@nickname} all the way to the office door. The teacher turned around and asked, "Student Aigis, do you have any other questions?" Aigis replied, "I have memorized everything you just said. Also—were you helping me out just now? Thank you." Pausing slightly, Aigis continued, "I would also like to ask, are the weapons you mentioned similar to my configuration? Which aspects are similar specifically..."
It seemed the teacher did not expect Aigis to say this. Pausing for a second, the teacher answered, "Not really. You and those are different." Then, the teacher seemed to blink (due to the hood and mask, it was impossible to be certain) and said, "However, if you need equipment maintenance, you can discuss it with Closure; she should be able to help."

One of the sticky notes attached to this page: Per Dr.{@nickname}'s request, Closure's "technical exchange correspondence" is appended to this file.
Second sticky note attached to this page: Amiya, there's no need to black out Closure's complaints about me in the letter; being misunderstood as some technical secret would achieve the exact opposite effect. Student Aigis uses non-Laterano replica firearms; recording it as such is sufficient.

handbook.char_4218_aigis.story.5.text.text:
After participating in the confectionery hall's volunteer practice, the transfer students would occasionally spend their leisure time there. Aigis seemed quite fond of sweets, but not out of a preference for the taste. She put it this way: "Through this period of observation, I have come to understand the reason why Laterano people are so passionate about sweets."
"I've noticed this too; it seems to be because Laterano abounds in sugar crops..." This was Amada's view.
"Eh, isn't it because Laterano people have a sweet tooth that they grow those crops in the first place?" This was Yukari's perspective.
"So it's still a culinary tradition after all..." This was Yamagishi's guess.
"No, the key lies in energy supply efficiency," Aigis stated with absolute confidence. "Sugars are the primary and most direct energy source for the brain. Consuming sugar supplies energy to the brain at the fastest possible speed. That is why Laterano people favor sweets so much; they possess an absolute advantage as energy-supply substances."
"..." This was Makoto's comment.
As Aigis affirmed her own thought: "As expected of Laterano, orderly and exceptionally efficient."
Yukari's expression was somewhat helpless. "Efficient, sure, it's efficient... As for 'order,' don't Laterano people have a different understanding of it than we do? Although Laterano has a lot of 'rules,' things like the 'Public Building Demolition Ordinance'... Rules like that are definitely something our world would never have..."
Unaware of Yukari's critique, Aigis seemed to begin pondering another question: "However, there is one thing I do not understand. Earlier, when Ms. Keira and Ms. Idita were arguing, they said that sweets are the memories of Laterano people. If sufficient energy powder is added to sugar-free ice cream, it would become a more efficient food, and everyone consuming it would form corresponding memories. In that way, wouldn't sugar-free ice cream with energy powder be able to replace sweets?"
Amada furrowed his brow, pondering Aigis's words, while Yamagishi said somewhat uncertainly, "Um... memory and memories aren't entirely the same thing, actually..."
Aigis remained somewhat puzzled, but Makoto nodded at this moment.
"'Memory' and 'memories' are different, I see... No, I need to think about this further." In the end, this is what Aigis said.

handbook.char_4218_aigis.story.6.text.text:
Information regarding the Requiem Mortuary incident remains undisclosed, but this did not prevent the transfer students from forming good relationships with the two mortuary deacons they met during volunteer practice. On a certain day off, the transfer students and Giada went to help Julio—who previously lived in the Repatriation Apartment—move to his new home. Aigis was very enthusiastic about this, stating, "Leave the luggage transport to me; it will be foolproof.
The problem lay with Julio. Upon arriving at his new residence, he unpacked the luggage he brought back from Columbia, successively pulling out a set of marbles, three sketchbooks, two cushions, and a broken ribbon flute, wearing an expression of utter astonishment. He seemed to have no recollection of more than half the items inside his luggage, leaving Aigis to wait as Julio verified them one by one.
Aigis was quite baffled by this: clearly these items were not essential to Julio's life, so why carry them all the way back to their home country? She added that, provided sufficient energy, she herself could survive in most environments on her own without any external possessions.
Julio apologetically explained: he was in low spirits when leaving Columbia and only hastily packed some items at an Executor's reminder, so he hadn't paid attention to what got put into his luggage.
"However," Julio said, "I still have to thank him. If I had just left these things behind... I would probably regret it now." Looking at those boards, sketchbooks, cushions, and flutes, he wore a nostalgic smile.
Before Aigis could continue questioning, a knock on the door interrupted them. The visitor was a light-blond Executor. Julio warmly greeted him, introducing him as the aforementioned Executor and mentioning that he had invited him to join the housewarming dinner. Recalling Julio's earlier explanation, Aigis directed a question at the Executor:
"Mr. Executor, did you remind Mr. Julio to pack these items because they were necessary for the return journey?"
"No."
"Do you understand their purpose?"
"No."
"...Then why did you have Mr. Julio carry these items? Isn't traveling light more efficient?"
"I agree. I alone am sufficient to ensure the safe return of this citizen to Laterano. But upon returning to Laterano, the citizen must still continue his life, and he might need items whose purpose I do not understand. Therefore, from the standpoint of an Executor, I fulfilled my duty of reminding him."
Though Aigis's doubts were not entirely resolved, she seemed to greatly appreciate the other party's working style, conversing happily with this Executor known for his poor communication skills.
From the look of it, although the volunteer practice failed to provide Aigis with career guidance references, it at least helped her make a friend.

handbook.char_4218_aigis.story.7.text.text:
At Dr.{@nickname}'s suggestion, the transfer students visited the Sanctorium together before leaving Laterano.
According to the rules of the Sanctorium, people can pray to the relics—or rather, "make a wish"—through spray-paint graffiti. Upon arriving, the transfer students felt somewhat apprehensive, though the atmosphere here was far more relaxed than expected. Amada felt a bit uneasy about the idea of graffitiing on the relics, but Yukari straightfowardly comforted him: "Just follow local customs. Look, the graffiti on top is already piled many layers deep; we should just do it the Laterano way." While spray painting, Yamagishi observed the relics closely for a moment, and afterward, asked Dr.{@nickname} in a low voice, "Doctor, this... is indeed a machine, right?" The teacher paused to think, then told her, "It doesn't matter anymore."
Makoto did not spray paint a wish on the relics; he smiled at Dr.{@nickname} and said something softly. The teacher nodded in response.
The teacher handed the spray paint can to Aigis, who was standing at the very back, and asked, "Do you have a wish you want to make, Aigis?"
Student Aigis took the spray paint can, but seemed a bit hesitant. She looked toward the relics, gazing at the colorful hues on their surface. From this vantage point, it would be difficult for an ordinary person to fully make out the text and patterns, though perhaps Aigis could.
She finally stepped forward. Unlike the Laterano people who left striking and vibrant graffiti, she seemed only to write a small line of prayer.
Returning to her companions, she handed the spray paint can back to Dr.{@nickname}. Although the teacher had asked about Aigis's wish earlier, the teacher did not press further. Everyone has moments like this, where certain wishes are meant only for oneself.
Student Aigis seemed to want to ask something, but ultimately didn't speak up. She looked back at the relics as sunlight pierced through the dome and fell upon her. Perhaps she already knew that the relics would not answer.

handbook.char_4218_aigis.story.8.text.text:
There are far too many mysteries surrounding Aigis for me to know where to even begin... Let us start with her identity. Aigis and her companions made little effort to conceal it: Aigis is not an ordinary human. Or perhaps "not human" is more accurate, given that she refers to herself as an "Anti-Shadow Weapon." That being said, keeping her true nature under wraps has become my job... Ah, thank you for your understanding and assistance, my old friend. The decree from the Sixth Bureau helped a great deal.
As for the true nature of these so-called "Shadows" and S.E.E.S.'s operational plans against them, these youths have not shared much with me. I suspect, however, that this is simply because their own access to information is quite limited. The good news is that Aigis has confirmed the "monsters" appearing in Laterano are not Shadows. I have roughly narrowed down the potential nature of these creatures into five main hypotheses, which you will find in the attached file. After careful consideration, I believe the most likely outcome is that the "monsters" will cease all activity once they depart, or enter an entirely unobservable state.
Truth be told, I am far more concerned about the state of these children than I am about Shadows. They are all still very young, and should be enjoying a peaceful, tranquil life at school. Instead, they have already grown accustomed to facing danger and fighting Shadows, treating it as a duty they must shoulder. For Aigis, who calls herself an "Anti-Shadow Suppression Weapon," perhaps this is only natural. But in my eyes, she possesses a genuine, precious life just like any other child, and deserves the chance to experience its true value—whether here or after she returns home. I hope she finds the life that belongs to her, and that one day, no one will ever call her a "weapon" again.

handbook.char_4219_yukari.story.2.text.text:

Teacher's Comments: Yukari Takeba is an intelligent, friendly, gentle, and cheerful student. She excels at communication and possesses a strong sense of independence. In our Firearms-Style Armament courses, her archery left a deep impression on the instructor. We hope that when facing difficulties, Yukari will feel comfortable accepting help from her teachers and peers as we work together to build a warm, harmonious class built on mutual aid.

handbook.char_4219_yukari.story.4.text.text:
Yukari quickly integrated into school life in Laterano. On her very first day, she exchanged contact info with the class monitor. By the third day, she had learned a shortcut from the dorms to the school building from Stitch in the tenth grade. By the fifth day, the auntie at the tuck shop already knew her name. Through joint practice with the archery club, Yukari even made a few friends she could talk to in other classes and years.
She also became a bridge for other students and the transfer students' small circle—naturally picking up the slack when Makoto Yuki fell silent, and deftly smoothing over the awkwardness whenever Aigis asked a strange question. Amiya once wondered why Yukari adapted to her environment so quickly. Yukari just shrugged and said, "Ah... probably because I have some experience with this? It's not my first time." For some reason, her smile carried a hint of self-deprecation. Perhaps catching the slight worry in Amiya's eyes, she quickly recovered her usual cheer: "Don't worry, all that experience came in handy after all, so there's nothing to fret about."

handbook.char_4219_yukari.story.5.text.text:
Because she enrolled late, Yukari missed the opportunity to experience the careers she was interested in during volunteer practicals. Though Yukari herself didn't mind, Amiya—who had grown close to her—always felt a tinge of regret. That regret was incidentally remedied.
One day, while Yukari and Amiya were out shopping at the supermarket, they were intercepted by a Liberi friar carrying a bow and arrows. The friar invited them to model for some magazine advertisements. "To break into the school tuck shop's supply chain, we must raise awareness of our monastery's bread among the students...!" So the Liberi friar claimed. Amiya seemed to recognize the monastery the friar came from, and with her encouragement, Yukari agreed to take on the job alongside her.
Later, two massive baskets of monastery bread arrived at the dorms as payment, and their companions finally learned of the incident. "The friar looked so pitiful when he begged... Besides, it's just photos, i-it's no big deal anyway! Alright, enough about that, let's eat some bread!"—The photo on the dorm's noticeboard of a blushing Yukari waving a loaf of bread was apparently taken right then.

handbook.char_4219_yukari.story.6.text.text:
Following their volunteer practicals, the transfer students befriended two deacons they met at the Requiem Mortuary, and Yukari was no exception. Hearing that Giada volunteered at Requiem chapels outside the mobile city in her spare time, Yukari accompanied her on one of her days off.
Resting in a field of flowers outside a Requiem chapel, Yukari asked Giada, "I remember Miss Giada mentioning something... In the past, Laterano didn't have Liberi funeral directors. Is that also a Laterano rule?"
"There is no such rule."
"Then it's some sort of social consciousness...?"
"'Social consciousness'... perhaps. After all, Liberi cannot resonate, and in the past, people truly believed they would struggle to take charge in settings like funerals."
"Even if someone works hard to learn, like Miss Giada... does that not help? Perhaps I don't understand Laterano, but 'because you are a Liberi, you cannot do this'—things like that just feel a bit unpleasant to me." Yukari's expression turned complicated.
Giada offered a wry smile. "It's probably not as severe as you make it sound... Though I have thought that if the Law hadn't undergone such changes, I never would have had the chance to become a funeral director now... Thinking that way might be a bit selfish, though."
"...I don't think so." Yukari shook her head earnestly. "Perhaps the events regarding the Law provided an opportunity, but it was because Miss Giada has always treated the work of a funeral director with utmost sincerity and effort that you were able to make it happen, no?"
She continued, "Liberi are Lateran residents too, aren't they? When circumstances change, different people can bring forth different strengths... This is a change Miss Giada brought about herself. At least, that is how I see it now..." She suddenly waved her hands in a panic. "Oh, why am I suddenly talking about something so solemn..."
Wearing a rare, gentle smile, Giada said, "Not at all. You are entirely right, and I will remember your words."

handbook.char_4219_yukari.story.7.text.text:
Yukari once tried to ask me a question.
Because the clinic was already closed for the day, I took Yukari—who had just finished training—to a hospital where an acquaintance of mine worked to pick up some pain-relief spray.
When we arrived at the examination room, my doctor friend was still seeing the last follow-up patient. The patient's daughter was waiting outside, and the Executor who usually accompanied her was seemingly absent, so we sat and chatted with the child for a bit. Upon learning that Yukari was a "transfer student from Higashi," Cecilia curiously rattled off a string of questions. Yukari answered them brilliantly, deftly avoiding exposing her "mysterious origins" while satisfying the child's curiosity. Children are often much sharper than adults; they can sense from a momentary hesitation or a forced choice of words whether their interlocutor is being sincere or simply patronizing them—a vigilance born of vulnerability. Yukari understood this vigilance, as it stemmed from the same place as her own self-preservation, which allowed her to build a gentle, unspoken rapport with a child like Cecilia. In less than ten minutes of conversation, Cecilia had already taken a liking to her "foreign big sister."
But when Cecilia turned the conversation toward her own mother, Yukari fell unnaturally silent. To make matters worse, Cecilia noticed her silence, and the second half of the question—"Where does Big Sis Yukari go when she goes out with Mom?"—faded away into a mumble. Fortunately, Failla emerged from the clinic at that moment, giving Yukari a natural opening to change the subject.
With a smile, Yukari accepted Cecilia's invitation to "go get sweets together next time," and watched the hand-in-hand mother and daughter leave the hospital. Her mood was clearly dampened.
"Doctor..." she asked, her voice so soft it sounded like she was talking to herself. "If a child feels a certain way toward their mother..."
She didn't finish her sentence. I pretended not to hear and simply reminded her that it was time for us to go see Dr. Kal'tsit for the pain-relief spray.
I didn't think she needed anyone else to provide the answer to that question. The right solution for one person is not necessarily right for another. Anyone can choose not to love anyone, and vice versa. I believe that one day, Yukari will find the answer she is looking for.

handbook.char_4219_yukari.story.8.text.text:
Like the other members of S.E.E.S., Yukari Takeba possesses the ability to summon a "Persona." But unlike Makoto Yuki and Aigis, she is not wrapped in layers of mystery. Fundamentally, she is much more like an ordinary middle schooler, which for a time left my investigations spinning their wheels. Still, by piecing together information gathered from multiple avenues, I was eventually able to reach a few conclusions.
Yukari joined S.E.E.S. to uncover the truth behind her father's death. As a result of investigating an accident from many years ago, she found herself swept up in circumstances that led her to join S.E.E.S. She has her reasons for fighting, and burdens hidden deep within her heart that she must face and untangle entirely on her own. However, one thing is certain: the truth she pursues has no bearing on your concerns or mine. Broadly speaking, she possesses a strong motivation to return to her original world, and once S.E.E.S. confirms the location of the door, Yukari will return home alongside her companions.
...I hope she learns the truth she seeks, and I hope that truth does not disappoint her. While I know nothing of her father's past, it is hardly uncommon anywhere in this world for the actions of the older generation to drag the younger one into a maelstrom of fate. I imagine her elders would never have wished for this, yet they were powerless to stop it... Even if our paths crossed only by chance, my old friend, join me in offering our blessings to these children.

Koromaru, companion of our class student Makoto Yuki. Unanimously recognized by class members and specially registered as an honorary student.
According to his companions, Koromaru is a Pelico beastkin. Locals in Laterano rarely see beastkin as willing to spend long periods of time in human company as Koromaru, and his intelligence and empathy have left a deep impression on many teachers and students alike. Most specially, Aigis shares a deep bond with Koromaru; she is able to understand the meaning of his barks and helps him communicate with others. Koromaru thus quickly integrated into the class and showed a keen interest in board games. He actively watched a class friendly chess match, earning himself the title of "Koromaru the Victorious."

handbook.char_4220_kormr.story.4.text.text:
In the contest for Koromaru's school hours, our class achieved an undisputed victory, a feat well worth recording in the class calendar.
Our competitor was a class in the elementary division of St. Marcheso Comprehensive School, the very class attended by classmate Ken Amada. Their class representative argued that the elementary division was where Ken and Koromaru first enrolled, and though Koromaru was never formally registered as a student, he should in principle be considered a member of the elementary division. Therefore, out of Koromaru's five school days a week, the elementary division should claim three. Our representative pointed out that the middle division has a higher proportion of outdoor courses, and the area for extracurricular activities is significantly larger than that of the elementary division. Considering Koromaru's physical and mental well-being, the middle division is far more suitable for him.
With neither side willing to budge, the argument gradually devolved into a war of honor between the elementary and middle divisions—until Koromaru himself stepped in to end the chaos. With the help of classmate Aegis, Koromaru expressed his wish to spend Monday, Wednesday, and Friday at the middle division, and Tuesday and Thursday at the elementary division. The elementary division representative burst into tears of excitement, though fortunately Koromaru promptly stepped forward, cuddling up beside the representative to soothe their emotions and avert the rumor that "students of our class are bullying elementary schoolers." Let us thank Koromaru.

*One of the sticky notes attached to this page: But Teach, Koromaru spent the entire day on Friday in your office. Shouldn't that be mentioned?
*Second sticky note attached to this page: This is a promise between Koromaru and me. It's fine, it doesn't detract from our class's victory.

handbook.char_4220_kormr.story.5.text.text:
Though the members of S.E.E.S. themselves cannot explain it, Koromaru truly possesses the ability to summon a "Persona," making him an important combat force within S.E.E.S. Aside from that, he is basically just... an intelligent and friendly Pelopsian here. My old friend, I know you might have some questions; of course Koromaru differs somewhat from Pelopsians, but this really is the most fitting "identity" for him. We should truly be grateful that they came to Laterano rather than Bolívar.
As for the question of his stay, you certainly needn't worry. Koromaru will travel alongside the other S.E.E.S. members, and he has no motive whatsoever to remain in Laterano. The students at the school are quite fond of him, but children are still young, and their treatment of Koromaru carries a hint of "chasing after novelty." Thus, I promised Koromaru that if he needs to, he may come to my office to rest. This is admittedly a bit of selfishness on my part, for I truly enjoy Koromaru's company. It is a kind of... rare familiarity. Perhaps he feels the same way? I have never asked.
In my time with Koromaru, I have gradually come to realize that he seems somewhat sensitive to the matter of "farewells." And we, too, must eventually part ways... Still, he has his companions by his side, so he shouldn't be too sad. I hope so, at least.

handbook.char_4229_aphris.story.4.text.text:
[Letter to Headquarters HR]
Affected by the current situation, more than half of the Columbian faculty and staff at Lumines University (La Unida Branch) have successively evacuated Bolívar. Fortunately, with the enthusiastic assistance of our Academic Affairs liaison, Ms. Rachel, we successfully completed the credentials verification for Operator Mueller. It has been confirmed that her records of enrollment, graduation, and employment entirely match the onboarding information she submitted—she indeed entered the university's Applied Originium Arts major at the tender age of twelve, and obtained her doctorate four years later, remaining at the institution as faculty ever since.
Equally surprising, however, is that this "prodigy" Originium technology researcher published only three academic papers during her eight years of teaching, with an even sparser record of attendance at academic conferences. While Bolívar has long been embroiled in strife and its overall research environment falls short of Columbia proper, Operator Mueller's work ethic is genuinely somewhat concerning.

[Audio Log]
Slacking off? No, Mueller's performance in the Engineering Department is nearly flawless. Whether it is tricky experimental data analysis, equipment R&D follow-up, or subsequent modifications, she handles everything with ease. I hear she even promised the Medical Department to open a "Journey into Originium Science" mini-class in the wards. Look at her, she hardly seems like the type who has lost heart in research and has been using the exact same teaching document for seven years!
You say she used to teach at Lumines University? And at the La Unida Branch? Heh, then the situation gets a bit complicated. Let me think how to explain this... *Ahem*, this matter goes back some thirty or forty years.

Lumines University is located in the Max Columbia District and was among the first higher education institutions established after the Federation's independence, supplying a large number of STEM talents to various departments and industries. In the early 1940s, the school was formally placed under the jurisdiction of the Columbian Department of Defense, acquiring a heavy military-industrial hue from then on.
In the mid-1960s, with the promotion of the "Preemptive Containment" strategy, the school's Development Planning Department established its first branch in La Unida under the jurisdiction of the Bolívar Allied Government. As soon as the news broke, scholars from all walks of life voiced their opposition. Pressured from both within and without, various faculties back at Lumines University's main campus sent successive letters to the president, delaying the construction of the La Unida Branch. However, backed by the Department of Defense and the Allied Government, the branch's research funding and compensation remained highly competitive, prompting many cash-strapped Columbian researchers to still choose La Unida in pursuit of their ambitions. By the early 1980s, the branch's development was fully on track. Yet due to the early controversies surrounding its establishment, quite a few researchers on the Columbian mainland still hold certain prejudices against the research output of the La Unida Branch.

handbook.char_4229_aphris.story.5.text.text:
The enemy falsely labels this operation an "evacuation." They publicly claim that everyone evacuated from the north were purely civilians. But upon inspection, we found that a large number of True Bolívarian soldiers had in fact been mixed in. They are continuously massing toward the south, attempting to launch terrorist attacks against several of our mobile cities and settlements.
That is correct, yesterday's attack against Tecoma, a specialized defense town of our humanitarian aid base, was a rehearsal for this very conspiracy. Officer, this is no mere "evacuation." Please be sure to convey this to the Allied Parliament: this is a long-planned "march."
—An audio recording played at a Columbian military tribunal following the Grand March incident

[Kroos's Operation Log]
To date, the Columbian Department of Defense has classified the recent series of extreme violent acts in Bolívar as a large-scale military operation disguised under the cover of civilians. The True Bolívarians have strongly condemned this action. The conflict between the two sides is highly likely to escalate once again.
A1 Detachment members Kroos and Beagle, along with several Rhodes Island Operators stationed at the Bolívar office, participated in this operation. Based on our observations, while there were indeed some soldiers among the evacuating columns, the core of this operation was unquestionably ordinary citizens affected by the northern blockade.

That night, Beagle, who was originally scheduled to rendezvous with us in the southwestern canyon, did not arrive on time. We only learned two days later that to rescue patients trapped in Tecoma, a Hound disease-prevention town belonging to the Allied Government, Beagle and several team members had temporarily rerouted there. What followed was this: the black flow swallowed the entire region, leaving many missing, and Beagle was among them.
A subsequent statement released by the Allied Government claimed that an army of True Bolívarians had attacked the town, causing an explosion in the storage depot and ultimately leading to the tragedy.
Yet I believe the situation was by no means so.

Kroos of A1 Detachment, requesting to return to the accident zone to search for Beagle. I can feel it, she must still be in that forest.

Near the river valley, I encountered the injured Ms. Mueller. Fortunately, she had not been infected by the black flow at the time. After simply dressing her wounds, we parted ways.

[Audio Log]
At the time, I accepted an invitation from a Columbian expedition team to serve as the team's information liaison, accompanying them to investigate near the Black Flow Forest. Little did I know that this trip would lead us right into the Dossoles turmoil and the Grand March that swept across all of Bolívar... and the team was scattered as a result.
My reason for applying to visit Rhodes Island? On one hand, of course, to express my gratitude; on the other hand, it is to find another suitable place to continue my research work. Judging by your expression, do you still have doubts? Heh, please go ahead and ask, I will answer everything truthfully.

handbook.char_4229_aphris.story.6.text.text:
It was originally an ordinary afternoon when Mueller walked into the ward right on schedule, preparing to give a class to the children. Upon entering, however, she discovered an unexpected guest among the audience—Miss Christine. After class, the lady curled her tail and circled around her several times. But just as Mueller squatted down and reached out to stroke the lady's chin, Miss Christine suddenly sprang up, eyeing her appraisingly.
Being rejected for pets by Miss Christine was nothing unusual, but the children in the ward took it strangely to heart. They co-signed a letter to the "Pet Enthusiast Exchange Club" at headquarters, hoping to secure a chance for Teacher Mueller to "successfully pet a small animal." Thus, Mueller received an invitation and attended the gathering.
At the gathering, a small tracking beast waddled over to her, wagging its tail. Mueller let the little fellow rub against her palm, and the two of them got along quite harmoniously. Curiously, however, Mousse's "cats" were somewhat wary of her—whenever Mueller reached out, they would quickly arch their backs and bolt out of her petting range, only circling around her from a distance. How strange; as a Feline, Operator Mueller seemed exceptionally unappealing to Feline beast kin. Could it be that she carried a scent they disliked? It baffled comprehension...
During casual chatter, everyone learned that Mueller had once raised a tracking beast. An Operator casually asked if she wanted to raise another, but she simply smiled and shook her head.

"Ever since I can remember, that little tracking beast had always been by my side. When I was five, my family moved to a small town in central Bolívar. But on the very day we arrived, the little tracking beast bolted into the woods outside the town and hadn't returned by nightfall. The next morning, I wanted to go into the woods to look for it, but the adults in town wouldn't allow it—after all, the forests of Bolívar conceal far too many secrets. Perhaps a warlord's garrison, perhaps a black market peddling contraband, or perhaps..."
"Wait! Weren't we talking about a tracking beast? How did this suddenly turn into such a terrifying topic..."

[Rhodes Island Ward Recording]
"You've come to listen to the lecture again?"
"The little sheep are sunning themselves on the deck, and the wolf pack has wandered off somewhere with that silvery-white young lady. Mr. Emperor recently brought some new records to check out at Rhodes Island, and also..."
(A drawn-out meow)
"Sigh, alright, alright, I will answer your question properly."
(A brief meow)
"The damage has already been done; wanting to repair it completely is impossible. But rest assured, Cadhoc has now found himself once again."
(A satisfied meow)
"Judging by your reaction... if I may be so bold: should I interpret your visit as concern for one of your own kind?"
(A puzzled meow)
"My condition? Heh, the same as yours, Madam. If possible, I hope you too can view me as a trustworthy... 'kindred.'"

handbook.char_4229_aphris.story.7.text.text:
"Lorenz"... There was once a Lorenz who was an old acquaintance of my teacher. Their research fields were similar, and they engaged in public exchanges on many occasions. But later, due to some scandals, that scholar vanished from academia.
—Aosta

"Doctor, I still have doubts about her identity. Her understanding of Originium far exceeds our expectations. I can sense a dangerous aura from her, and I worry—"
"Yet she has committed no oversteps whatsoever at headquarters... Very well, let us keep things as they are for now.
"No! We still need to have HR Operators check her file again! I must double-check ZOOT's encryption protocols as well!"

[Privilege Log]
At the strong insistence of Ms. Closure, we conducted a third review of Operator Mueller's resume. The re-examination results were no different from the previous two—there are no inherent issues with her information. Yet... it is precisely such a seamless file that arouses suspicion.
Following her surname, "Lorenz," we dug up a past event from Columbian academic circles:
In the late 1970s, an Applied Originium Arts researcher named "Robert Lorenz," at the young age of just over thirty, shocked the Columbian academic circle with several groundbreaking papers. Surprisingly, however, this brilliant scholar did not remain in mainland Columbia, but instead traveled far to Bolívar in response to a high-paying invitation from Lumines University (La Unida Branch). Following that, this prodigy became embroiled in a series of scandals. According to currently verifiable information, this "Lorenz" appeared to have a history of endorsing a controversial politician; was suspected of participating in a private foundation's illicit embezzlement of charitable donations; and even interfered in the domestic affairs of a domestic academic authority... Initially, these claims were treated as mere defamation, with some scholars even publicly calling for a rational view of a scientist's personal choices. But as rumors of "Robert Lorenz conducting illegal experiments in Bolívar" spread like wildfire, the young scholar quickly became a public target. Since then, this sharp new star of academia has never again been recognized by the mainland academic circle. One day in the late 1980s, word reached the outside world that he had presumably passed away.
Based on the materials at hand, we have been unable to find any definitive connection between this Lorenz and Operator Mueller. At present, we can find no explicit records of him establishing a family in La Unida either... The trajectory of his final few years of life is practically a complete blank. Yet we have always suspected that some form of connection exists between Operator Mueller and this Robert Lorenz.
Lumines University (La Unida Branch)—a campus that successively sheltered two "Lorenzes," must surely hide even more untold secrets. The institution itself seemingly serves as an elaborate veil draped over some more classified operation.

Doesn't this sound like a rather fascinating story? If possible, I truly hope some top director from Raythean takes a fancy to it and adapts it into a film. It would surely pull in a decent box office.
—A sticky note left on the Doctor's desk

handbook.char_4229_aphris.story.8.text.text:
Open your eyes, Tony, everything you see is real. Don't believe those bastards' nonsense; you are no "Little Robert" or "Little Lorenz." You have your own name, and you deserve your own life.
cyon You were born in Columbia, but because of some foolish things I did when I was young... and out of my own selfishness, you were quietly brought to Tecoma. Everything that happened afterward was just as you saw: once hypotheses were confirmed and theories put into practice, things here didn't get better; instead, they bred endless suffering and violence. I cannot answer why things turned out this way. I know I committed a grave mistake, yet I cannot make amends—when I clearly had no wish to drag anyone into this quagmire... I wanted to re-distinguish right from wrong, to rediscover morality, justice, and conscience, only to find that these hands of mine, which sought to touch the truth, were already stained with sin.
...But you still have a future, Tony. By whatever means necessary, you must leave Tecoma. I don't know what you will be like when you grow up, but I guess you will probably still be fascinated by science and full of passion for ideal models. If that truly is the case, then I pray for you... I pray that you will be different from me, that you will be far greater than me, capable of taking responsibility for all your own research and every decision you make.
Tecoma is permeated with lies everywhere, but your life is not. Tony, someone has truly loved you, and going forward, someone will surely care about your truest self. As for this computing terminal... After much thought, I have decided to leave it behind. The past has nothing to do with you; in the future, use it to record your own journey.
Oh, and the username is your name, and so is the password.

handbook.char_4230_mcnist.story.2.text.text: Mechanist, Elite Operator of Rhodes Island. He leads the R&D, manufacturing, and maintenance of Rhodes Island's weaponry, equipment, engineering facilities, and experimental apparatus, providing essential hardware support for operators across all departments.

handbook.char_4230_mcnist.story.3.text.text:

[Cell-Originium Fusion Rate] 5%

Operator Mechanist strictly follows the most standard protective procedures, and rarely removes his jumpsuit even off duty.

"Now you know how dangerous mechanical engineering as a hobby can be."
— Mechanist

handbook.char_4230_mcnist.story.4.text.text:
Mechanist almost never takes off his jumpsuit.
Of course, it's not like anyone really wants to look at his weed-like hair or his eyes, varying in size due to sleep deprivation, but we still feel more or less perplexed when he sits down at the dining table in his jumpsuit.
"For the convenience of plunging into work at any moment" was our initial guess. It is not hard to imagine how desperate a person who has just conceived a brilliant inspiration would feel if he found himself forced to complete a tedious set of jumpsuit-wearing procedures at the laboratory entrance.
However, with Mechanist's skills, building a device to help him put on and take off his jumpsuit quickly is not difficult—at least not difficult enough to make someone willing to endure all the inconveniences of wearing a jumpsuit all the time.
Later we learned that he wasn't "enduring" any inconvenience at all.
Inconvenient mobility? The hidden wheels and thrusters on the soles of his shoes say otherwise.
Too hot to wear? The built-in air conditioner, fans, and cooling patches solve the problem.
What if you need an itch scratched? There are two small mechanical arms in the jumpsuit, front and back, moving up and down along guide rails to reach every inch of skin except the soles of the feet.
And what if you need to show your face? Everyone should appreciate the scrolling display screens he sewed into his jumpsuit displaying vulgar Colombian slang, which he used when he returned to Columbia after many years and his mission happened to require him to enter the headquarters of Wolter-Cochinsky.
This layer of jumpsuit turned many problems into the situations Mechanist is best at solving—situations that can be solved by mechanical means.
If you praise him for this, he will politely indicate that he is simply doing things his own way. You won't see his expression, but you can hear the small mechanical arm inside the jumpsuit scratching his head for him.

handbook.char_4230_mcnist.story.5.text.text:
When Mechanist first appeared at our gatherings, he was not yet an Elite Operator.
Those weren't our best times; even when holding a gathering, few people could muster up any joy. You could tell from Misery's face—he would feel sorry for it, but every time he felt pessimistic about things, he would still wear that expression... as if everyone's days were numbered. Raidian would sometimes make "Little Tree" and "Little Ax" hold hands and spin around the table in time with the rhythm, but she used to dance herself. Logos would occasionally still try to amuse everyone with his weird incantations, but he was also very careful to avoid pulling off untimely pranks.
All that was left was the radio playing.
Right at that moment, Mechanist walked through us unconcernedly with his toolbox, and began to fiddle with the thermometer-like device on the wall. That was also one of the gadgets he brought from Columbia, but it seemed to keep breaking down. Every time we came to this gathering, we could see him fixing it.
He started tapping away, and the lyrics on the radio became indistinct, drawing attention instead to many other sounds, like Rhodes Island grinding over the gravel beneath us.
"Which of you on earth is alternating between generating heat and refrigeration?" he suddenly turned around to ask.
Logos looked sheepishly at the flask in his hand, half of which was frozen and the other half still burning.
"Thermodynamics preserve us," he muttered, tossing over a roll of insulation cloth.
"Our time isn't up yet," I looked at him, and suddenly blurted out unprovoked, "At least that guy is still fixing his stuff."
Everyone laughed.
— Ace

It was only after Mechanist joined that we gradually began to develop the habit of organizing various games and competitions.
He was a better hitter than many Rim Billiton natives, and better at imitating song and dance vaudeville acts than many Lateranians. He knew every brand of cigarette card and their corresponding betting rules, and was proficient in the puzzle games published in science fiction magazines. How he used these methods to please investors in the past, we do not know; but the way he skillfully used these things to please himself was witnessed by all. More often, he didn't mind creating a set of absurd rules of his own—the paperclip fencing tournament or the non-burnt potato cooking contest—and dragging everyone into his chaotic gambling den.
Depending on the timing of the gathering, we would cry, laugh, argue, and fall silent, but Mechanist was always doing the same thing. If we weren't in the mood to play with him, he would be with the structural principles; if three people were needed, he would add the mechanical arm behind him.
When the gambling ended and the alcohol had fully dispersed in his body, he would begin to write poetry—writing poetry like throwing a physics monograph into a crucible and stirring it. His recent poetry ended like this:
"Whoever exhibits continuous symmetry in the flux of time, the conserved quantity in their life is life itself."
He often uninvitedly translated my words, and I should occasionally translate his poetry. Like a farmer whose rules of life are demarcated by the timing of sowing, the method of sewing, and the craft of slaughtering Originium Slugs, who will not doubt his life because of any drastic changes on this earth, a person whose rules of life will never be broken will never lose the meaning of his life.
I should perhaps add another joke: Mechanist never realizes he is such a person.
This indeed gives all of us peace of mind. Occasionally, we would all unprovoked blurt out this sentence—
"Our time isn't up yet, at least Mechanist is still reciting his poetry."
— Logos

handbook.char_4230_mcnist.story.6.text.text:
This is my fifth year working at the Patent Office.
My daughter said at school again that she wants to do my job when she grows up, and her teacher came to tell me, so I could only offer as much sincere praise as I could. After all, next time, I'll have to ask the teacher to distribute our questionnaires to the whole class.
Every day's work unfolds in a capsule experimental cabin of less than ten square meters. The technical department sends the filtered patents to our hands, and we, "like little children who just got new toys," apply these technologies to all occasions we can think of. Having obtained the anti-vibration bearings of mobility scooters, why not try using them for the rotating shaft of a cotton candy machine?
The questionnaires come in handy this way. The knowledge brought from the Institute of Technology is put aside, and we first have to understand all possible needs that might exist in this country. Heavens, I even know the "class division" of elementary school students comparing stationery.
It is said that we are turning a patent that perhaps no one will ever pay for into ten or twenty "applied patents" that are bound to be put into production and make a profit. Of course, the ownership of these "applied patents" has nothing to do with the inventor of the original patent, nor with us—they belong to Columbia.
— A researcher at the Colombian Intellectual Property and Patent Office

Resolution passed, and power poured into the Patent Office like a breaching dam. Let the Administration deal with objects, the Patent Office confiscates ideas.
Standard equipment for a Patent Office investigator includes two ballpoint pens, a dozen patent application forms, and a portable door-breacher. With these, they can precisely locate all technical designs not certified by the Patent Office. Unauthorized production? Illegal. Selling blueprints? Illegal. Just using it yourself? There is potential legal risk.
All truly valuable designs must become patents, after which the researchers of the Patent Application Department can multiply and transform new application methods based on them. As for whether inventors actually need the "protection" of patents, it doesn't matter.
One can imagine how much dissatisfaction this resolution triggered when it was just passed. The Patent Office urgently needed to handle a case with enough deterrent force to emphasize their authority.
Wolter-Cochinsky sent a suitable victim, an Aegir engineer who was too obsessed with maintaining his own work and fell out with them. His studio was turned upside down; everything except the designs delivered to the company—those he tried to produce privately for profit, those he gave to his alma mater as teaching aids, and those he used for himself—were confiscated, and he was heavily fined.
Of course, the Patent Office failed to confiscate much in the end, and that Aegir fled with his blueprints to an overseas medical enterprise. But thanks to this, the Patent Office was able to wildly spread rumors that his identity was suspicious and his motives impure, thereby substantiating the justice of the confiscation work.

[An Application for Resignation from the Ship]
Once the adaptive temperature control system is officially put into use on this ship, I will return to Columbia.
Thanks to your esteemed company, all the technologies I brought have been applied reasonably, which means the purpose of my coming here has been fully achieved.
I am aware that returning to Columbia is a dangerous thing for me, but my intuition drives me to focus on the other side of things.
Many people compare the country to a machine, either to state political claims or to hurl political criticism. But after this time, I can indeed clearly feel—
Columbia is a machine.
I still won't give it half a shred of recognition, but its operating logic... has that pure rationality and efficiency unique to machinery. Whether I am a victim of it does not affect this point. I don't like conspiracy theories, but if someone now says that the operation of this country is fundamentally driven by a machine, I wouldn't be surprised.
I am curious.

This application is pinned under Mechanist's workbench and was never submitted to the HR Department.

handbook.char_4230_mcnist.story.7.text.text:
[Excerpt from Unobjective Resume, p.04]
Mechanist did think about leaving Rhodes Island to return to Columbia. At that time, he didn't know Whitesmith yet.
Whitesmith approached him of her own accord. Mechanist's first words at the time were to ask her why she didn't replace her wheelchair with an automated one, when she clearly had the ability to build one.
Tacit understanding between geniuses, I guess. He didn't need to know her to tell she had molten iron in her veins, and she didn't need to have met him to figure out he had gears in his brain. Whitesmith knew her own physical condition and understood that the Rhodes Island workshop needed a successor, and Mechanist arrived just in time.
She didn't expect Mechanist to be extremely unskilled at this job. When he first took over the equipment maintenance and manufacturing work for Elite Operators, not a single one of his works could be used properly. The compound bow he painstakingly polished for three days fell apart in Stormeye's hands in three minutes, and the flying bowstring almost severed half of Stormeye's horn.
The next day, a plastic basket appeared at the door of Mechanist's workshop, containing a bottle of whiskey. For a while after that, Mechanist never left the workshop, and a bottle of wine would appear in the basket at the door every day. Mechanist never drank during working hours, and he said these were saved until he solved the problem. When that time came, he would drink all the wine he wanted to drink in these days in one breath without missing the chance.
It's not hard to understand why he was so obsessed. Even though he kept his helmet on, everyone could tell that the truth he had believed in for more than twenty years had shattered at Rhodes Island. He couldn't understand why his perfect designs, which seemed to be the embodiment of physical laws, appeared so clumsy in the hands of Elite Operators. He iterated his designs at a rate of five drafts a day; of course, the result still failed to meet his wishes.
Whether taking over someone else's engineering or adjusting machinery based on humans was still too unfamiliar to him at that time. He didn't understand that those unruly Elite Operators actually only needed a little quirky "flaw".

[Excerpt from Unobjective Resume, p.11]
By that time Whitesmith's condition was already very poor, and the workshop was being managed entirely by Mechanist. But one day, she suddenly said she wanted to forge something again.
She lit the forge for the first time in a long time, originally just wanting to repair someone's weapon, but Mechanist told her that all weapon repair requests had been processed. For this final time, he hoped Whitesmith's forge would burn only for herself.
All the equipment she needed was modified by Mechanist to just the right degree, requiring manual operation for each step, but requiring only very small movements for each operation. Even Whitesmith, who had difficulty moving her arms at the time, was able to operate it.
A small pendant, Whitesmith forged it from day to night, and from night to day, but what she lacked least was sincerity and perseverance. Mechanist watched from the side all along, knowing that no matter how long it took, it could only be completed by her own hands.
Finally, when the pendant was finally finished, Mechanist shaved off a facet of the gem. The glowing light reflected by this gem would never fall perfectly in its exact center, but this way, it looked more like Whitesmith's eyes.
After this, Whitesmith's forge could never be lit again. That night, Mechanist drank all the wine at the door of the workshop by himself.

"When we first met, I asked her why she didn't replace her wheelchair with an automated one. She said, because her hands could still move.
"This is the reason I stay at Rhodes Island."
— Mechanist

handbook.char_4230_mcnist.story.8.text.text:
Yes, this is structural principle, Mechanist's proudest work.
It is far from as cute as it looks. We rarely use "extremely strong territorial awareness" to describe a machine, but applying it to structural principles is truly most appropriate. The engineering department's vehicle parking lot originally had no assigned parking spaces; whether it was Bagpipe's small tractor, Earthspirit's sidecar motorcycle, or those operation platforms, they could park wherever they wanted—until the structural principle came into being. No one knew how it selected that parking space, but as long as anyone approached its parking space, it would stiffen its neck and adopt an aggressive posture to drive away the intruder.
Mechanist refuses to admit when sober that structural principle has any personality to speak of as a machine, but everyone knows why it has this personality. Just as he always fails to realize that his poems are all depicting himself, he also fails to realize how similar structural principle is to him.
Yes, Mechanist is a person with "extremely strong territorial awareness". Initially, his "territory" only contained unshakeable physical laws and all those proud works of his that he allowed no one else to touch. But now, he can no longer tell what is in his "territory"; there are more people he cares about in it, more principles he recognizes, and perhaps more things he wants to accomplish.
Since he could disregard consequences to defy the federal government's penalty order to protect his work back then, now, for the people and things he cares about, he will surely not step back half a step.

"Just like how he set twenty defense programs for structural principle?"
"Just like structural principle stiffening its neck to guard its parking space."
