handbook.char_4231_clemnt.story.4.text.text:
[A Trial Feedback, Clemencia to Weapon Design Institute]
Hard work. Shrinking the ship-borne cutting tools to this extent must be quite laborious work.
Based on the trial experience of this round, there are not many problems left with its functionality and usability. The previously discovered situation—high-frequency vibration of the blade leading to wrist fractures in the user—did not happen again (the fracture has also healed, thanks for the previous care).
When cutting most inorganic materials, its performance is very stable. However, when facing Seaborne tissues, the Grade IV weapon technology mounted on the sword cannot take effect stably, and some tissues can still slowly regenerate after being cut.
Improvements are hoped for.
In addition, I also want to ask you for a favor—engrave a sentence on the sword body.
Let's just engrave this one:
"You are the salt of the earth."

[An Etymological Study, written by Clemencia at the Language Design Institute]
"You are the salt of the earth," a phrase of praise originating from Iberia. Like most Liberi living in Iberia today, this phrase originally came from Laterano, where "You are the sugar of the earth" was its original form.
"You are the sugar of the earth"—the first saint of Laterano exclaimed this from the bottom of his heart when he first grew sugar crops on the earth. This sentence was recorded in "The Acts of the Saints" and passed down from generation to generation in Laterano. Considering that Lateranian people have a sweet tooth, it is not hard to understand why this sentence carries a praising meaning.
After spreading to Iberia, this phrase quickly changed. In those years when Iberia's salt industry flourished and the palates of Iberia's people were gradually tamed by the sea, the "sugar" in this phrase naturally evolved into "salt". The taste and economic value of salt together endowed this phrase with a strong complimentary meaning, and with the prosperity of the salt trade, this phrase also spread to various countries in the southern part of the continent.
"You are the salt of the earth," land dwellers thus praised various wonderful things.

[A Dialogue Record, Clemencia and a Researcher at the Weapon Design Institute]
"Archon Clemencia, I don't quite understand. If it is a phrase of praise by land dwellers, shouldn't it be engraved on gifts presented to them? Why engrave it on a sword?"
"To remind myself."
"Remind... what?"
"If I tell you that salt is the most important seasoning on land, would you find it strange?"
"Seasoning with salt? How is that different from unseasoned?"
"We certainly cannot assume that everyone treats salt with disdain like we do just because we live in a huge pot of saltwater soup. I should at least remember this... especially in situations where I need to draw my sword."

handbook.char_4231_clemnt.story.5.text.text:
When I arrived at the dressing room, Archon Clementia was already seated in front of the mirror. Her hair on the right was not pinned back as it usually was, and the stray lock just barely covered her eyes. I guessed that she probably couldn't see herself in the mirror that way.
I asked her how she wanted her makeup done. She thought for a moment, then asked me, "What should a human look like?"
I was taken aback.
Then she raised her head, smiling as she told me she was just joking, and to do it the way I was used to.
——A makeup artist from the Public Activities Administration Office

An Archon doesn't always need to show their face in public, or rather, most of the time it's only those few Archons who do. The scientific Archon of Myrialium has never made any public speeches; all of their views are conveyed through the technical Archon, Clementia.
In fact, the occasions where Clementia appears in public extend far well beyond Myrialium. Large-scale national plenums, technical exchange exhibitions facing all cities, and academic development synchronization programs watched by every citizen are frequently hosted by Clementia. Today, the person required to represent Aegir and establish diplomatic relations with terrestrial nations is also Clementia.
Of course, it's not as though no one has ever proposed using simulated avatars and electronic voices to handle these tasks, but such proposals were only ever overwhelmingly vetoed. A civilization that invented a simulated personality with autonomous thinking capabilities more than two hundred years ago still installs simple logic modules capable only of passive responses in various mechanical products to this day. That can only explain one thing—it places far too much value on the irreplaceable nature of humanity.
When it was initially assessed that Clementia could serve as an Archon, the Development Planning Office incorporated her image into their considerations. Aegir needed someone to speak on its behalf, and this person needed to look kind, friendly, calm, and rational.
Most importantly, she needed to look like an ideal "human," an image that would naturally allow the public to identify with her simply out of the pride of being born human.
They believed Clementia's image, deportment, and speech all met the requirements. At least, that was the conclusion reached by several research institutes in the humanities after a prolonged, systematic field survey.
She must have felt lost, being told without warning that she was the ideal "human" form.
——A liaison officer from the Public Activities Administration Office

Therefore, whenever Clementia had spare time, she would go act as a "model." Of course, not to find the painters at the Visual Arts Creation Institute, but rather to come to our Paleontology Research Institute.
We would map her head fins, tail, and skeletal structure, and she would cooperate with us in performing various physical movements so it was convenient for us to record her movement patterns.
Combined with her complete gene sequence provided by the Genetic Science Institute and the literature provided by the Prehistoric Research Institute, we were able to conduct a relatively thorough restoration of the ancient species to which Clementia once belonged (referred to by prehistoric civilization as the "Giant Manta Ray"). Thanks to the vast amount of research materials enthusiastically provided by Clementia (primarily coming from her own person), we were even able to produce complete skeletal and muscular modeling for this species, and simulate its mode of action on the computer.
I am not clear on why Clementia is so passionate about this, but most of the time I would venture to say she simply looks...
She simply looks like she is thoroughly enjoying the fact that she is a manta ray.
——A researcher from the Paleontology Research Institute

handbook.char_4231_clemnt.story.7.text.text:
People like us who travel around Aegir year-round can all easily tell which city Clementia has handled.
If you walk into a room and find a small metal bottle placed on the table, that is Clementia's handiwork. The compressed gas inside the bottle was collected from your previous residence, and if you are willing to open it, your new home will smell exactly the same as the old one.
However, during the time I was temporarily stationed in Myrialium, what she prepared for me was a scented candle. That was just ordinary incense, completely unrelated to the place I had stayed before. She probably knew that there was always the lingering scent of the Seaborne in the Abyssal Hunter Research Institute, and she also knew that I didn't like that scent.
Oh, she even knew I liked candles.
I don't know why she goes to all this trouble, but I guess it might be to give her city a bit more of a "home" feel.
If anyone applies to move to her city because of these things, I wouldn't be surprised at all. At least, if I weren't an Abyssal Hunter, I definitely would have done just that.
——Laatentiya, Abyssal Hunter

Everyone knows what it means for us to apply to move to Myrialium at a time like this.
There is a destructive urge inherent in human nature. When a child squashes a worm to death for the first time, they must be happy. But what about the second, third, and fourth times? What if all a person could do for their entire life is endlessly think of one, and another, and yet another way to kill worms?
Our lives are just like this. Trapped in an endless war, using all our creativity to design ways for the Seaborne to die until our noses and mouths are blocked by the stench of Seaborne flesh. Then, we bring our own children into the laboratory and have them continue doing the same thing.
Some people can accept it, but... not everyone. Not everyone. Rather than designing ways for the Seaborne to die, I just want to be able to decide the manner of my own death.
Thalassa Plan is a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity. We all know Myrialium will be a one-way trip. One city, two under-strength legions, from the mainland to the coastline... At least people will view this as a glorious sacrifice.
There are quite a few others who think just like I do. We spread out the time and place of submitting our applications as much as possible, and made up plenty of different versions of our reasons. As long as the Development Planning Office cannot see our intention to seek death, they have no reason to reject our application to move to Myrialium.
...
Thank goodness, they approved it.
——Avitus, citizen of Myrialium

The Development Planning Office could not possibly approve any of their applications. We rejected them on the grounds of insufficient qualifications, thinking the matter would end there and not spawn extra complications.
Archon Heratia had given instructions that any news regarding this matter must be kept strictly confidential from Archon Clementia... It's not hard to understand why. Having managed Myrialium for all these years, if she were to find out that those people came to her city purely to seek death... At least, according to Archon Heratia, this "is not conducive to her maintaining a good mental state that meets mission requirements."
Yet the one who ultimately meddled in this matter was none other than Archon Clementia. She bypassed our approval process and transferred those people into Myrialium through special requisition channels under the guise of mission necessity.
...She knew. She had known all along. She simply accepted it.
——An evaluator from the Development Planning Office

handbook.char_4231_clemnt.story.8.text.text:
The evaluation report from the Development Planning Office has already used rather worried language to remind us that everything Clementia has done since becoming Archon has exhibited a strong sense of purpose. To quote the report directly, she seems to have "completely stopped doing anything purely for her own life."
This condition did not alleviate in the slightest even after she went ashore. We would occasionally notice her flipping through Columbian comic books with great interest, or holding a telescope to observe birdbeasts in the wastes of Rim Billiton. Of course, we would also always find corresponding meeting schedules for them on her calendar—government representatives from Columbia, or heads of the Rim Billiton Mining Union.
In fact, when we finally decided to arrange a conversation to briefly communicate with her regarding her work stress issues, what she talked about with our HR operator was that operator's most beloved, uh, semi-fictional historical novel.
After an hour of conversation, that operator walked out of the conference room and swore up and down that we didn't need to worry about Clementia at all, but we could tell from the corners of her mouth which she couldn't keep down that she was simply happy to have rarely found someone with the same hobbies. But how are we supposed to know whether Clementia genuinely enjoys that, or if her condition has become so severe that she would even make completely unnecessary preparations for such simple conversations?
The supervisor went to find her alone later. Discovering that the supervisor quickly bypassed the topic she had initiated, Clementia no longer evaded the question.
"All those things, reading comics, watching birdbeasts, and reading semi-fictional historical novels... Do you genuinely enjoy doing those things?"
"I am glad to have the opportunity to come into contact with them. They really are all very interesting.
"Then what is it that you truly want to do yourself?"
"Doing nothing, does that count? Just floating on the water somewhere. Swimming is too much trouble, so just floating."

handbook.char_4232_hbound.story.2.text.text: Nacho, an Aegirian islander, proficient in hydrographic surveying and geographic modeling. After the port salvage project concluded, he joined Rhodes Island through Clementia's recommendation, stationed in Iberia as a cooperative operator to assist Rhodes Island with hydrological observation, climate monitoring, and other work in the coastal areas of Iberia.

handbook.char_4232_hbound.story.4.text.text:
"So, is this considered practice makes perfect?"
When the curious HR operator asked this question, Nacho's spherical detection device was scanning a corridor on Rhodes Island, where a young patient's flying toy had gone missing nearby. That piece of equipment was originally used in Iberia to sense maritime climate in addition to detecting seabed structures. On the fifth day after Nacho arrived at Rhodes Island, he stood outside the Engineering Department and made a modification request to the first Engineering Department operator who took the initiative to greet him. When the Engineering Department operator asked why, he sheepishly produced three "Lost Property Retrieval Notice Letters"—now this device could scan the basic spatial conditions of any building and environment, and Nacho naturally became a volunteer at the Lost and Found.
"I don't know why I lose so many things in a day either; it wouldn't do to cause trouble for the operators at the Lost and Found..." Nacho squatted down and placed the scanning panel in front of the young patient. The child poked the glowing spot—her toy was stuck in the ventilation duct. Nacho lay flat on the floor by the wall and reached in to grab it.
Nacho is undoubtedly a likable person. Although he looks like a cold current hovering over the Iberian sea and has a severed arm, he is very happy to help out. However, whenever he encounters troubles he needs to deal with, he isn't very good at asking others for help. After older operators go on missions with him, they turn into his "guardians" in a sense.
"Oh!"
"Oh! You got little Raina's toy?"
"I might know why I lose so many things."
"Why?"
"When working at the Rea-Iberia Salvage Center, technicians would wear diving suits when going underwater. Even if things were lost, they were only lost inside the diving suit, and you just had to dump them out. That way most personal items wouldn't get lost. However, I always felt that working this way was too inefficient, so I would stick my prosthetic limb out of the diving suit and operate directly in the seawater, and as a result I would lose bolts, haha..."
"Haha?"
"And speaking of the prosthetic limb, I know how to get the toy back now. Could I ask you to use the weather orb to distract little Raina's attention?"
Nacho unbuckled the clasp of his prosthetic limb. The detached arm operated a few times under Nacho's remote control and climbed into the duct like a pod-limbed organism to retrieve the toy. Until it was reattached to Nacho, the HR operator's look of horror had not faded.
"Sorry, I didn't think it would scare you too?"
"...I suppose I understand why you have so many 'guardians'; now I really want to join them. Even if it's just a prosthetic, attaching and detaching it puts a burden on your body all the same. Please don't do that so casually again."
"The parts of this prosthetic limb once helped Supervisor Clementia recover Rea-Iberia, making me an 'hero' in the eyes of some Iberians. This title makes me feel very, very unsettled. I'd rather use it to retrieve a flying toy and be little Raina's 'hero'."
"..."
"Hm? Why aren't you saying anything?"
"..."
"I shouldn't talk either? Just accept your hug? O-Okay..."

handbook.char_4232_hbound.story.6.text.text:
We almost threw hands.
When we learned that Rufina's grandson was safe and sound and that she was willing to raise him, we were actually all very happy. During those three months when she was agonizing over not knowing what to name him, we all helped think of names. Yet no one expected that what she ultimately decided on was actually an Iberian name.
It's not that islanders can't have Iberian names; too many of our compatriots have forgotten our ancestors' naming rules and had to switch to Iberian names instead—there's nothing to that. But Rufina? She was the one person who couldn't possibly do such a thing.
When all is said and done, the reason we gathered here, discussing how to resist and how to struggle, was all because of Rufina. If not for her, we probably would have just stood by and watched compatriots get stabbed, burned, and nailed to lamp posts one after another.
Rufina never accepted this reality. The islanders had made contributions to Iberia, and the islanders had not brought disaster to Iberia—she spent the latter half of her life trying to prove these things. She told every one of us to remember everything about Aegir, because if we don't remember, no one else ever will either.
And then, she gave her own grandson a quintessential Iberian name?
Those of us who were the most radical even suspected that she had betrayed us. That night, no matter how people reproached her, Rufina said nothing. In the end, everyone's voices grew hoarse from arguing, and she dropped a single sentence:
"Whatever I am trying to prove, it has nothing to do with that child."
After that, she never took action with us again.
——An islander who once participated in sabotage operations

"Name?"
"Nacho."
"Surname?"
"Uh... García López."
"Is the paternal surname first or the maternal surname first?"
"Uh, no. My parents both had Aegirian names, and my first and last names were both made up out of thin air by my grandmother. They're the most common and ordinary ones, to make me look more like an Iberian..."
"Understood. Then would you like to change the registered name? We can handle that.
"N-No need. The current name is fine, I like it very much. Although it actually can't change anyone's view of me at all, but... the name itself is great.
"All right.
"But, if possible... I'd still prefer it if the files didn't have a surname, and just said 'Nacho'. That way, it's better for everyone..."
"Better for everyone? Why?"
——HR Information Registration Office, a dialogue

What Nacho borrows the most here is always technical manuals, and sometimes he borrows novels too. But recently, he has been borrowing fewer and fewer novels and more and more scripts.
Looking at the books he returns, it isn't hard to understand why. For all the novels he reads, although he tries very hard to smooth out the pages, you can still tell that the first few dozen pages are much fluffier than the back; he must have flipped through the front parts over and over again. But in the case of scripts, the traces of repeated thumbing are limited strictly to the cast list right at the front.
I'm guessing Nacho must be someone very bad at remembering names. For novels, he has to flip back to see who is who after reading two pages; by contrast, the advantage of a script is that all the characters' names are neatly listed right at the very front.
Ha, if everyone's name in a book were as short and easy to remember as "Nacho," he would definitely be able to read much more easily.
——Librarian of the Rhodes Island Library

handbook.char_4232_hbound.story.8.text.text:
Nacho's arm condition is concerning.
After promotion, his sense of responsibility seems even stronger. Nacho actively participates in various affairs between Rhodes Island and Iberia, and hydrographic surveying already puts a burden on his prosthetic limb. Now the number of times he comes to you for prosthetic limb maintenance is increasing...*
"Is it okay to slowly shoulder the responsibilities of new work at my own pace? But—"
"No, no, no, I'm not worried that Rhodes Island won't issue extra pay, nor am I worried about the decline in lubricating oil quality. I'm only working overtime because—uh, I'm only working overtime because..."
"Even if my pay increases, the things I can do and have to do also increase, but the time we spend together is still just this one hour of prosthetic limb maintenance every month, isn't it?"
"If working overtime can increase our maintenance time... Ow, please don't knock on my head..."
"What else do you want to do besides maintenance? Together with me?!"
"I-I haven't thought about it yet... I'll think of something very soon."

handbook.char_4234_pedro.story.2.text.text: Pedro, a Bolívar native. Once drafted by several different True Bolívar forces, he generally participated in combat as a guerrilla fighter or intelligence operative. After the Bolívar Grand March, he left the True Bolívar forces and is currently cooperating with Rhodes Island, assisting with certain intelligence operations.

handbook.char_4234_pedro.story.3.text.text:
Imaging tests reveal clear organ outlines in this operator with no abnormal shadows detected. Originium particle tests in the circulatory system show no abnormalities, and there are no signs of Originium infection. At this stage, the operator is confirmed to be uninfected.

[Cell-Originium Fusion Rate] 0%
Operator Pedro shows no signs of Originium infection.

[Blood Originium Crystal Density] 0.08 u/L
Operator Pedro rarely comes into contact with Originium.

I have doubts regarding this part of the record. When he arrived, he was carrying a custom crossbow made specifically by True Bolívar forces. If you ask me, that thing was essentially an Originium dirty bomb, and even storing and carrying it carried a certain degree of risk; it was only disposed of when we processed and inspected hazardous items. And yet, he was clearly extremely familiar with that thing—how on earth is this considered "rarely coming into contact"?
— Logistics Department Operator expressing doubt over recorded content

handbook.char_4234_pedro.story.4.text.text:
Quite a few warlords and guerrilla factions among the True Bolívar forces are not opposed to raising or employing child soldiers, and Pedro appears to have been one of these child soldiers. We have no authority to excessively interfere in this, particularly given that True Bolívar outwardly claims all child soldiers volunteer to resist foreign invaders and defend their homes.
According to disclosures from Operator Pedro, he indeed volunteered to participate himself, with his reason being "hoping even one more person could survive"; as for his repeated transitions between various warlords and organizations, it was because "fallen comrades said there is no future for Bolívar to be seen here."
We feel concerned for the plight of these child soldiers. We also regret to note that before being swept onto the battlefield by slogans and mobilization orders, they clearly failed to receive an education sufficient to allow them to fully contemplate and comprehend their own lives and this land.
Even more heartbreaking is that we lack the standing to simply condemn the ways those warlords treat their own compatriots. Many of these child soldiers lost family and homes in the invasions of internal and external hostile forces, ultimately reaching a dead end with no hope of salvation in sight, making enlistment almost their only way to survive. The soldiers who trained them were born in the same turbulence; if these youths manage to survive famine, disease, and the flames of war and grow into adulthood, I fear they themselves will become the ones training the next batch of child soldiers... The invasions endlessly staged for selfish gain will eventually cease, and we will remain forever dedicated to safeguarding the dignity of every individual's life.

handbook.char_4234_pedro.story.5.text.text:
In truth, during the course of combat testing Operator Pedro, there were a few peculiar interludes.
Although the capabilities he demonstrated were practically indistinguishable from other armed personnel who had received standard combat training—I mean, while this might not be easy for a child soldier either, it wasn't all that bizarre. The bizarre part lay in those aspects difficult to encompass merely through parameters: aside from the most cutting-edge ones, he was proficient in using a variety of standard-issue weapons, and his accuracy with handheld ranged strike weapons like crossbows was shockingly good, even capable of precisely hitting the bullseye of a moving target during transit. Furthermore, all handling of infiltration operations was extremely clean and crisp, leaving no flaws. While there might indeed be geniuses in such matters, his situation seemed more akin to someone with an extremely high level of proficiency rather than a genius... I can hardly believe what kind of lives these child soldiers lead.

Postscript: Don't let me catch any of you laughing after learning the relevant test results, wearing an apple on your head to harass an operator of this age. Suction-cup arrows won't fly either; Kroos wouldn't pick targets for teasing as tactlessly as you lot.

handbook.char_4234_pedro.story.6.text.text:
We originally always believed that before coming to Rhodes Island, Operator Pedro likely had little opportunity to receive a proper general education, but judging from his performance in these classes, that does not seem to be the case. We specially arranged some test content for him that exceeded the curriculum, and he was able to correctly answer a portion of those questions. Furthermore, he learned things he was unfamiliar with extremely fast, though he lacked somewhat in imagination and was not adept at handling things he had never actually seen and certain abstract concepts. Overall, however, he remains a youth who deeply gratifies and endears himself to the instructors.
However, solely on questions concerning modern history relating to Bolívar, Iberia, and Columbia, Operator Pedro frequently failed to answer correctly. We are uncertain whether this is the influence of concepts instilled by True Bolívar or if certain traumatic experiences prevent him from accepting textbook teachings. But at least for the present stage, we believe he should not be forced to accept textbook history; rather, he should be given an open space, which might prove more advantageous for his growth.
Additionally, we noticed that Operator Pedro seems remarkably inept at proactively discovering things he wants to do, but as long as tasks that need doing are arranged for him and he is told the reasons why, he suddenly lacks no enthusiasm whatsoever. This cannot simply be attributed to a numb mental state, nor do we truly understand the genesis of this personality. Yet we still hope a youth ought to have at least a few things he proactively wants to do, even if it is just playing to his heart's content.

handbook.char_4234_pedro.story.7.text.text:
Operator Pedro is somewhat abnormal. I must clarify that I have no intention of expressing prejudice, but as I did when organizing other operators' files, when I attempted to observe and record his life and interpersonal relationships at Rhodes Island, I indeed ran into difficulties. He seemed as though he did not exist here at all, though I suppose this phrasing is also inaccurate; rather, were it not for the nature of my work, I would never even think of him, and this is likely the case for other operators as well.
I have heard rumors and anecdotes of legendary intelligence operatives, saying they are able to make people unable to accurately recognize or recall their faces, but Operator Pedro is somewhat different. Operators who have had contact with him can clearly remember his features, and his performance has no out-of-touch qualities whatsoever; Operator Pedro is even willing to cooperate to the utmost with all reasonable requests directed at him, yet the operators also express a certain confusion—they seem completely unable to perceive Operator Pedro's likes and dislikes during their interactions, and even harbor the illusion that both they and Operator Pedro had politely distanced themselves from each other starting from some point in time. Meanwhile, those operators who collaborated with Operator Pedro in combat exercises stated that despite perfectly completing all projects together, they had not the slightest recollection of when or how they achieved coordination with him.
After reviewing some activity logs and combat footage, I am quite certain Operator Pedro has not been subjected to isolation from other operators, nor has he intentionally distanced himself from us, but when I suddenly realized today that I had nearly omitted the observational report on Operator Pedro's interpersonal relationships, I could not help but find it rather odd.
Recording these is not intended to advocate for some sort of collective mindset; I entirely agree that demanding an introverted person to become "genuinely" fond of group activities is essentially an act of bullying, but Operator Pedro's situation still inevitably causes me some concern. If possible, I hope to obtain some more professional opinions and support.

handbook.char_4234_pedro.story.8.text.text:
Death has no value, nor does it have meaning, not even the most magnificent death. A warrior's death does not, a coward's death does not; a good person's death does not, a sinner's death does not.
Is an old person's death any less regrettable than a child's? Is an infected person's death any less regrettable than an uninfected person's?
No death can bring about anything. A righteous courtier sacrificing themselves to kill a tyrant does not equal bringing about justice; a brave soldier sacrificing themselves to kill a general does not equal ushering in peace.
People commemorate sacrifices made for ideals for a long time, and I have witnessed those sacrifices with my own eyes.
Yet did they not want to live? Did they not want to continue practicing their ideals, and then on the day they were realized, embrace every comrade? Did they truly resign themselves to falling before the dawn arrived, accepting the memorial rites of their comrades and becoming the most memorable name among this group of people?
I have heard that answer from their lips, but no one would want to know. A person who lives and succeeds is ultimately criticized for a mediocre remaining life or slandered with exaggerated flaws, whereas the dead are not.
Yet if that is the case, how is this any different from praising death and chasing after death? If that is the case, where lies the value of life?
If accepting death as a price and a bargaining chip is considered maturity, then I might perhaps prefer to be a bit immature.

handbook.char_4235_thumpy.exam.retestRec.text:
"Failed the Originium Arts theory test, failed the Originium Arts practical test as well, the only thing that reached standard level is adaptability... How many times have you had to retake tests now, shall we just...?"
"Ahahaha! Th-Then how about I try again with grandma's pocket watch?"
"Mm... This pocket watch is indeed a very powerful casting unit, but... *cough*, if you can't learn it, using even the most powerful thing is useless."
(Sound of despairing collapse)
"Aiya, don't be too sad; I had this exact same feeling when I was studying math and physics. Some things you just can't learn... you simply can't learn them, after all."

handbook.char_4235_thumpy.story.2.text.text: Sanby from Great Spring in Rim Billiton comes to Rhodes Island to receive treatment for Originium infection and, through the recommendation of Operator Angelina and in accordance with her own wishes, joins the External Affairs Department as a Defender operator to provide assistance to Rhodes Island.

handbook.char_4235_thumpy.story.3.text.text:
Tissue-slice imaging reveals blurred outlines and abnormal shadows in the operator's internal organs. Test results show abnormal Originium particle levels in the circulatory system, confirming her as an Infected at this stage.

[Cell-Originium Fusion Rate] 3%
Operator Sani has a small amount of Originium crystals on her wrist.

[Blood Originium-Crystal Density] 0.17 u/L
Sani's condition has been well-controlled and is currently stable.

Upon learning that height measurements wouldn't include her ear length, Sani was even more pleased with her short ears, which were just like her grandmother's. However, after being caught hiding height-increasing insoles, Sani looked even more miserable than if she had eaten a damp, soggy dried carrot.

handbook.char_4235_thumpy.story.4.text.text:
"(Extremely softly) Yellow carrot, green carrot, pink carrot, red carrot."
"Alright, Sani. What was the last thing he just said?"
"Hehe, I heard it! It was 'pink carrot, red carrot'!"

On the day of her employment physical examination, Sani demonstrated astonishing hearing. Whether it was echolocation, frequency range testing, or even identifying the exact line uttered by an operator whispering Rim Billiton's most difficult tongue twister, <it>The Carrot</it>, in the far corner of another room, Sani excelled at all of it. Consequently, more and more people gathered to watch the hearing test. Closure crowded over with her equipment to have Sani listen to where a fault might be located, and after troubleshooting the issue on the spot, she enthusiastically invited Sani to join the Engineering Department as a maintenance engineer. Medical operators busy in the neighboring room brought over different hearing aids to see if she could tell the difference in sound, and Red Bean came over with her guitar to have Sani listen to the differing tones of various strings, while Old Well strolled in carrying a dice cup, asking if she could tell what numbers were rolled...
This minor chaos finally ended when everyone—even without needing exceptional hearing—could hear the loud rumbling coming from Sani's stomach. Everyone reached into their meal cards to buy food for Sani to express their gratitude, gathering together to eat while continuing to discuss Sani's potential career paths. At that moment, a few Adnachials suddenly looked puzzled: "Is there some kind of factional dispute between long-eared and short-eared Rim Billiton people?"
Sani's first reaction was to reply, "Not at all," but after a moment's thought, she changed her answer to, "Maybe there are, but I've never paid attention to it." She proudly added, "That's because my ears look exactly like Grandma's!"

handbook.char_4235_thumpy.story.5.text.text:
The thirteenth Originium Arts adaptability test ended with the usual "Standard" score. Sani found that whether she went up holding her grandmother's casting unit pocket watch, recited Originium Arts theory backward and forward, asked Angelina for special training, or even learned from Alchetto by kneeling on the ground before the test to beg her casting unit to work, nothing could change the reality that she had zero talent for Originium Arts: "How is it that I didn't inherit Grandma's talent for Originium Arts?!"
Although whether Originium Arts adaptability is heritable remains medically inconclusive, and the notion that a grandmother would pass certain traits down to her granddaughter lacks theoretical backing, Sani had always believed that her grandmother had passed down many things to her, citing her iconic short ears and pale pink hair as strong evidence.
Based on this "inheritance theory," Sani attributed many things to having inherited her grandmother's strength and wisdom, or achieving them by following in her footsteps: just like her grandmother, she had rescued a trapped person from the underground all by herself, traversed the entirety of Rim Billiton, and reached the legendary Southern Bounds said to possess the most beautiful scenery...
Yet Sani knew full well that these feats had nothing to do with genetics. Furthermore, there is a very long gap between "wanting to do something" and "actually doing it," and Sani had already crossed that distance, step by step growing into an even more formidable version of herself.

Sani had just suddenly asked the Medical operator if she thought she might have also inherited her grandmother's height, and whether she could still grow a little taller? Well... Grandmother Inala must have been among the exceptionally gifted among the Catur in terms of both height and build; judging by Sani's current age, she probably wouldn't be able to grow as tall and large as her grandmother!

No way, no way, no way! I can still grow taller!
—Sani

handbook.char_4235_thumpy.story.6.text.text:
Living in a heavily populated nation, the people of Rim Billiton are accustomed to giving everyone around them distinct nicknames so they can quickly tell apart individuals with the same name. Sani had many such nicknames.
When she was little, she was called "Little Doll." Because she was tiny, her ears were tiny, and everything about her was small. Whenever she wanted to play with the others, they would laugh and say, "Little Doll is too small, she can't play this," and leave her out. Sani wasn't very happy about it, because she wanted to play too, and she felt she could do it. That's why she didn't like that nickname.
Later on, Sani acquired a few other nicknames: "Good Head," derived from her ability to remember the names of almost everyone in town; and "Switchboard," simply because she served as the switchboard operator in the town... Sani couldn't say she disliked those at the time, but she grew increasingly envious of her grandmother's nickname: "Pathfinder Inala"—how majestic, how impressive! "If only I could have a nickname like that..." Sani said she used to imagine such things from time to time.
That wish was soon realized.
Returning to Great Spring from the Southern Bounds, Sani was pleasantly surprised to find that at almost every station she passed through, people still remembered her and even gave her new nicknames:
"Big Mouth"—earned from screaming and shouting all the way while she and Jacinta flew in to rescue their friends; "Warm Heart"—given by the people of Artichoke Village to thank her for speaking up for Amelia, which got their comms tower repaired; "Short-Eared Tani"—given by the miners of Sun Valley Industries, who kept her grandmother's prefix to thank her for rescuing their repairman; and "Little Warrior"—used now by Sani's parents and dozens of her relatives, because their brave little Sani accomplished what she set out to do and fulfilled her dream; as well as "Pathfinder"—the current Sani has stepped out of Rim Billiton, exploring the vast expanse of Terra alongside our field squads, seeking out habitable places for more of the Infected.

Hehe, I almost forgot to mention where the name "Sani" comes from! It's because I used to stamp my feet thump, thump, thump, so Grandma gave me this nickname meaning "Thumping Feet." My family uses it when they want to make me happy, so I chose it as my codename!
—Sani

handbook.char_4235_thumpy.story.7.text.text:
Recently, an operator out for a midnight snack reported in panic that she had encountered a supernatural event: she saw a backpack moving through the empty, deserted corridor all by itself. Soon after, several others stepped forward to say they had experienced the same thing—though after reviewing the security footage, everyone realized it was actually just Sani running down the corridor on an emergency mission.
Indeed, that oversized backpack is many operators' first impression of Sani. However, anyone who has watched Sani in the training room—refusing to give up no matter how many times she trips or gets hit by her own pack, bitterly practicing over and over how to coordinate with her gear in combat—or has gone on field missions with her and seen someone so tiny sling that backpack onto her back and get straight to work, would find their impression shifting away from the giant backpack toward Sani herself, someone small in stature but forever bursting with drive and courage.
As for the source of this courage, even Sani herself couldn't quite explain it. After all, she had always been the most timid one in her family: a prime example often brought up by her parents was her more than thirty failed attempts to run away from home, each time getting scared right back inside the town limits.
Perhaps because there were so many children in the household, busy with the countless problems generated by countless kids every day, everyone overlooked the tenacity behind Sani's thirty-plus attempts, never imagining she would try a fortieth or fiftieth time—until she truly walked out of the town and reached the Southern Bounds. It was only after Sani returned that they even discovered she knew how to drive. She knew her family didn't pay much attention to her dream of going on an expedition, but harboring a resolute determination to leave, she simply taught herself in secret: the first day, she screamed in fright at the roar of the engine; the second day, she cried so hard her tears flew against the windshield due to failing to control her speed; the third day, she almost got her vehicle flipped over by a geyser because she miscalculated its eruption timing, leaving her too terrified to step back into a vehicle for three days... Yet without ever having left her hometown before, and without any experience driving on proper roads, Sani practiced her driving skills step by step until she could take turns with Angelina on Route Zero, performing at a level where no one could tell she was a beginner, and without a single mishap.
Thus, the source of this courage perhaps lies in Sani's unparalleled determination to accomplish what she sets out to do, or perhaps because she has already failed countless times in places where no one was watching, she is no longer afraid of failing again, knowing full well that she will simply try once more until the day she succeeds.
Who knows, the protagonist of the next legendary tale might just be herself—
This is one of the most fervent expectations of the author, whose ears have already developed calluses from all those "Grandma stories."

handbook.char_4235_thumpy.story.8.text.text:
Sani recently made a sudden request to visit a certain uninhabited zone in Rim Billiton.
There are no livable settlements there begging to be explored, nor any breathtaking scenery. The only thing setting it apart is likely the fact that for hundreds of miles around, there isn't a single soul, plunging the nights there into absolute, pitch-black darkness.
After packing her bags, Sani set off. Following several days of grueling travel, she finally arrived at her destination. Pitching her tent, night finally fell.
Darkness flooded the entire space like a rising tide; the only sources of light here were the headlamp on Sani's head and the twinkling stars scattered across the sky. Pulling out her binoculars and camera, Sani aimed her lens at the faintly glowing starry sky and began searching.
She swept past the Milky Way, past the morning star, past countless beautiful seas of stars, until she found that familiar starlight: those two pink and gold stars keeping each other company finally appeared with crystal clarity before her eyes.
Sani pressed the shutter, capturing the beautiful night sky.

handbook.char_4236_tmslot.story.2.text.text: Telecommunications technology engineer whose research results have been applied to Rim Billiton's remote communication systems. Now joining the Rhodes Island Engineering Department to provide technical support for Rhodes Island's base remote communications.

handbook.char_4236_tmslot.story.3.text.text:
Tissue-slice imaging reveals clear outlines and no abnormal shadows in the operator's internal organs. Test results show no abnormal Originium particle levels in the circulatory system, confirming her as non-Infected at this stage.

[Cell-Originium Fusion Rate] 0%
Operator Alchetto shows no signs of Originium infection.

[Blood Originium-Crystal Density] 0.12 u/L

During her physical examination, Medical operators discovered that the feathered beast accompanying Alchetto everywhere was not a mechanical construct, but a lively, flesh-and-blood creature—one that could even mimic human speech.
It maintained a reserved silence despite the operators' endless attempts to coax it into talking, until it saw Alchetto being continuously comforted by a Medical operator to keep her from being nervous while she teared up. At that moment, the feathered beast finally opened its beak and uttered its first words: "Useless."
Alchetto's eyes welled up with even more tears!

handbook.char_4236_tmslot.story.4.text.text:
Operator Alchetto was timid for a long time when she first joined the Engineering Department, frequently asking whether she needed to brew coffee for the group leader or supervisors, or if she needed help organizing documents, and remaining uneasy even after other operators assured her none of that was necessary.
Closure—the "grand supreme direct boss" in Alchetto's eyes—took Alchetto by the hand on the second day after she completed her onboarding training and officially joined the Engineering Department, leading her into a laboratory specially prepared for her research into Rhodes Island's remote communication technology, fully stocked with all kinds of equipment. Not only did Closure patiently listen as Alchetto stammered through all her technical ideas, but she even stayed up all night alongside her when she ran into snags building the experimental setup to help finish the job. Having been through all of this, Alchetto finally relaxed completely.
Not only would she tell Angelina during meals in the cafeteria, "I really love it here!", and share with Jacinta and Tani in the dorms, "It's so wonderful here! I can do whatever I want!", but even the Procurement Department operators reported that the number of tissues Alchetto purchased to wipe away her tears had dropped significantly. Everything was moving in a positive direction, and everyone was thrilled to see Operator Alchetto blossom into such a lively and cheerful person.
Yet a few weeks later, we once again caught sight of Operator Alchetto sitting miserably in the cafeteria, eyes brimming with tears and looking utterly aggrieved. The HR operator rushed over in sheer panic to ask what was wrong, and Alchetto, holding back again and again, finally wiped her tears and blurted out the reason:
"My workload and overtime hours... how come they've multiplied several times over compared to before?! Waaah!"

handbook.char_4236_tmslot.story.5.text.text:
[Laboratory Security Footage]
"Operator Alchetto, we've scheduled a tour of the remote communication lab today. Just wanted to ask if you're busy right now?"
"...Operator Alchetto?"
"...Operator Alchetto, are you there...?"
(Footsteps)
"Waaah, sob...!
"Please, little bug; please, staff; please, communication core!
"Just work already, please go back to normal!"
"Operator Alchetto, why are you kneeling on the floor?! Get up, get up, the floor is so cold!"
"Sob! Please, just work properly!"

[Rhodes Island Barber Shop Security Footage]
"One pump of conditioner, two pumps of conditioner, three pumps of conditioner, four pumps of conditioner...!
"Wh-Why is my hair still so dry..."
"Oh, it's alright, Goldenglow, my hair has always been like this..."
"Miss Alchetto, please wait a moment while I go find some hair-repair oil. I'll definitely make your hair smooth and silky!
"By the way, Miss Alchetto, your hair color is so pretty! Everything else is brown, but these two braids and the bangs up top are pure white!"
"Actually, they used to be all brown... I guess whenever I'm stressed out, I start pulling on my braids, so they turned white..."
"Ah..."

[Conference Room Work Footage]
"Operator Alchetto, you're up next for the presentation. Please get ready!"
"O-Okay!
"De-Deep breath, don't be nervous, last dry run: Hello everyone, I'm Alchetto, here to present today, and my to-topic is, is...
"Oh no, I'm doomed, I'm doomed, I'm doomed!"
...
"Medical operator! Medical operator! Operator Alchetto's face looks completely frozen!"

During recent operator mental health wellness initiatives, the HR Department conducted a counseling session with Alchetto based on these pieces of footage. Topics included whether she felt under excessive pressure working at Rhodes Island and whether she needed assistance. But Alchetto merely told the HR operator, amidst blushes and apologies, that she felt her current state was much better than before, and those antics were just some leftover habits of hers.
Once the counseling concluded and Alchetto left the room, the HR operator noticed a few slender replacement communication antennas accidentally left behind on the chair. They must have been from right before she came to the counseling room, when Alchetto had been continuing her research in the lab.
True to the results of her psychological evaluation, Alchetto was far stronger and more resolute than she appeared—much like those tiny antennas. Although slender and seemingly on the verge of snapping at any second, they possess the power to connect cities to cities, and perhaps one day, nations to nations.

handbook.char_4236_tmslot.story.6.text.text:
HR Rumor 1: Longitudinal Red Inc. has a newly appointed head of engineering—an engineering director who, according to their CEO, promised to "revolutionize remote communication technology within a month."
HR Rumor 2: Three months have now passed since the Longitudinal Red Inc. CEO made that bold declaration.
HR Rumor 3: The Longitudinal Red Inc. engineering director was spotted sitting desolate and dreary on a curbside late at night after finishing overtime (later verified not to be the end of her workday, but simply stepping outside for some fresh air midway through her overtime shift).

Ever since Operator Alchetto resigned from Longitudinal Red Inc., both the rumors and their subsequent job postings made it abundantly clear that they were facing severe difficulties in achieving technological iteration. Meanwhile, Operator Alchetto—who might have otherwise been able to help them—was sitting right here in our Engineering Department office, browsing the latest Rim Billiton newspaper. The front-page headline read: <it>Amelia Repairs Every Single Comms Tower—How Did She Pull It Off?</it>
While the news article listed factors like timing, skill, and sheer luck, if you asked Operator Alchetto, she managed it simply because of a child's small, innocent wish.
Back when she was little, every morning after waving goodbye to her mother heading off to work at the mine, Alchetto had to wait an entire day and most of the night before she could tell her mother—who finally returned home after a late shift—about everything that happened to her. Sometimes, if she was too exhausted and fell asleep, she would always forget one or two things she had meant to share.
By the time she started school and later entered university, she had to wait even longer for couriers to deliver her handwritten letters to her mother at the mining site, while her frugal mother's replies took even longer to reach her. She would only find out her mother had fallen ill after she had already recovered, and her mother could only comfort her when she was away and lonely long after she had finished crying in secret.
"If only I could transmit the words I want to say to Mom a little faster," driven by this very wish, Alchetto traveled from the mine to the small town, from the town to the big city, and from the big city to the enterprise where she worked... Yet time did not wait for her. "I'm going to make something of myself and become Mom's pride."—This was the message Alchetto sent to her mother's terminal during the testing phase when the second-generation remote communication system successfully passed review. Her mother would never receive her messages again, but she knew that the test message would remain permanently stored in the system as initial data. It represented the fruits of her hard work and stood as an unwavering promise to her mother: whether ten years or twenty years passed, she would keep striving just as she promised, working hard to become a better person, a daughter her mother could rest easy about, and a source of pride.

"Mom, look, I did it... My name is in the newspaper!" After drafting the message and hesitating for a long time, Alchetto finally pressed send and dispatched the transmission.

handbook.char_4236_tmslot.story.7.text.text:
Speaking of Operator Alchetto's work after arriving at Rhodes Island, aside from her contributions to Rhodes Island's remote communications, one cannot omit her entrepreneurial venture with Operator Jacinta. However, Alchetto had been fretting quite a bit over this lately, as the "startup team" formed by the two of them kept running into a continuous stream of problems:
Take Laterano, their first stop, for instance. Though geographically close to Rim Billiton, the local customs and culture differed vastly from it. To get Lateranos to even listen to their pitch, the pair first spent time continuously tasting over eighty varieties of desserts to break the ice, then racked their brains to answer the question, "It would be even better if remote communication could be combined with Resonance," ultimately receiving a "we'll be in touch" reply from the Prelate. Or consider Victoria, where they spent days agonizing over social etiquette just to network with the local nobility, not to mention Sargon, where they were hauled off to observe a new round of chieftain selections before they could even get two sentences out, or Minos, where the locals insisted that remote communication was still slower than their long-distance running messengers, and Columbia's corporate enterprises cuttingly pointed out that their team "lacked the qualifications for partnership altogether"...
After hitting a brick wall everywhere, Alchetto was found secretly crying in the Engineering Department, agonizing over how to advance their startup, when Closure happened to pass by and shoved a massive tome she claimed she had poured her heart and soul into writing: <it>Methodology of Selling</it>. From then on, Alchetto clutched this booklet and pored over it constantly during meals and breaks, even begging operators to contact Bison in an attempt to gain entrepreneurial experience, while Swire was also reportedly consulted by her on multiple occasions...
Following tireless efforts, Operator Alchetto tremblingly took out the proposal she and Jacinta had prepared for days and began a trial pitch. Yet before the contents could even shine through, tears welled up in her eyes. Still, according to the Arc operator who happened to pass by the trial presentation, what Operator Alchetto wrote was actually quite impressive. After a post-discussion debrief, the audience ultimately decided to have Swire conduct special training for Operator Alchetto in her spare time, striving to instill in her enough presence and gravitas to convince anyone.
Though things look terribly rocky right now, perhaps one day, we might just find ourselves welcoming a newly minted, world-famous entrepreneur!

handbook.char_4236_tmslot.story.8.text.text:
Amelia thought carefully. It seemed the little fletching by her side had been with her for many years now.
It all started when she took a tumble as a child, sitting on the ground and crying. The little fletching wasn't very good at flying yet, and a gust of air flipped it over in mid-air, landing squarely on her head. Perhaps finding the texture of her hair quite pleasant, the fletching simply settled down and fell fast asleep. Amelia cried for a few more hours before finally stopping her tears when night fell, heading home while trying to comfort herself with, "Amelia, you cannot cry like a hopeless crybaby anymore." The fletching also seemed to have a sudden stroke of enlightenment, learning to mimic human speech before it even knew how to fly: "Chirp, chirp chirp!... Hopeless chirp chirp!"
Amelia wasn't particularly thrilled by this, of course, but having such a little animal by her side was still better than gritting her teeth and bearing things alone—provided the fletching didn't always pop up with a "hopeless" right when she was shedding tears.
Later on, when she went away to school, she assumed the little fletching would be scared off when she boarded the transport vehicle. Yet when she opened her package in the school dorm, Amelia found the fletching lying on its back, sound asleep. When she graduated from university and the headmaster presented her diploma, the fletching popped out from somewhere yet again, showing off a brand-new word it had just learned: "Chirp, truly amazing chirp chirp!"
However, the fletching only ever said that phrase this once, and Amelia even suspected whether it might have been an auditory hallucination on her part.
Later still, whether she was pulling all-nighters at the company or resting in her cheap little rental room where she hung dried carrots to dry, the fletching would always flutter its wings, fussing about in her hair to carve out a nest before settling comfortably inside to sleep. Even when she slipped away from the company to run herself ragged on repairs, even when she charged into the sandstorm alongside Angelina and the others, this little fletching had always followed right by her side. Only, during that period, whether out of shyness or greater consideration, it rarely blurted out nonsense when Amelia cried—though perhaps the reasons making her cry back then were different from usual.
When she came to Rhodes Island, the fletching naturally came along too. Faced with Angelina and the others staring in utter astonishment as the fletching ate and drank, Amelia finally had the time to properly explain that this little creature, previously mistaken by them as a heavy-duty fletching-shaped "little flying bug," was actually a living fletching.
Lately, however, Amelia felt that the fletching rarely said "hopeless" anymore. Perhaps it was because she rarely shed tears these days, or perhaps because there were far more smiles on her face now. So, when would the fletching say "truly amazing" to her once more?
Would it be tomorrow? Amelia felt a flicker of anticipation.

handbook.char_4237_jcinta.exam.originium.text:
Standard

After Jacinta used her small umbrella as a weapon and achieved commendable results in testing, Engineering Department operators drawn by the news conducted a thorough study of it.
This custom-ordered small umbrella her parents had commissioned was far more practical than it looked: built-in components could automatically launch and attack enemies once a button on the handle was pressed, while the ribs and canopy were crafted through special processes to be remarkably sturdy. It even housed a concealed communicator capable of directly contacting her bodyguard team, sufficient to ensure Jacinta's safety... Beyond all that, the materials chosen for the umbrella took Jacinta's physical stamina into account, making it extremely lightweight.
Just as the operators were marveling over the umbrella, Jacinta pulled a small folding fan out from somewhere inside it to cool herself off—had they even anticipated that need?

handbook.char_4237_jcinta.story.2.text.text: The daughter of the Campbell family, renowned mining tycoons of Rim Billiton, arriving at Rhodes Island for Oripathy treatment. Per her own request, she now provides assistance to Rhodes Island as a Pioneer operator.

handbook.char_4237_jcinta.story.3.text.text:
Imaging tests show blurred organ outlines and abnormal shadows in the operator's thoracic cavity. Granular abnormalities are present in the circulatory system, indicative of Oripathy infection. At this stage, the operator can be confirmed as an Infected.

[Cell-Fusion Resonance] 13%
Trace amounts of Originium crystals are distributed across Operator Jacinta's skin.

[Blood Originium-Crystal Density] 0.41u/L
Operator Jacinta's condition has been well-controlled in recent years, though the outlook remains less than optimistic.

Following a series of physical examinations and tests, Medical Department operators discovered that Operator Jacinta's condition and various physical metrics largely aligned with the thick stack of medical reports she brought along, yet indicators such as muscle mass and cardiopulmonary function showed inexplicable, significant improvements.
Medical operators originally intended to consult her on what specific training regimen could yield such results within a few months so it could be applied to all patients, only to receive the answer: "Crossing Rim Billiton twice."

handbook.char_4237_jcinta.story.4.text.text:
Tall, quiet, gentle, her skirt and cuffs forever immaculate and pristine... These were typically the first impressions Operator Jacinta left on everyone, and people had always maintained a polite and friendly social distance with her, fearing that excessive outgoing enthusiasm might offend or startle her—until that fateful day:
To enrich the patients' lives, the Medical Department decided to hold a singing contest in the garden. Anyone, patient or not, could sign up to take the stage and sing their favorite songs. Sign-ups flooded in overnight, and Jacinta even invited Sampi to join her in singing a Rim Billiton folk song, "Oh-Woo-Oh!". By the time their turn to take the stage arrived, dusk was already falling and the crowd's spirits were waning, yet the two of them enthusiastically introduced themselves and immediately belted out their song—
According to an Engineering Department operator stationed far away in another sector at the time, she was trying to quickly finish testing equipment stability so she could grab dinner, but for some reason, her level kept jittering. Puzzled, she finally decided to open a window for some fresh air, and a fiercely piercing voice burst into her ears—"The ears of a Catur~ aren't afraid of the blowing wind~ Oh-Woo-Oh——!♪"—she finally understood why her level was jittering, and was inexplicably infected by the singing, deciding to go check out the scene in person.
Thus, she saw everyone in the garden holding hands, dancing in chaotic, rather comical steps while laughing uproariously. Jacinta on stage was in high spirits—though her volume clearly couldn't match Sampi's—singing wildly out-of-tune lyrics, bearing no resemblance whatsoever to her usual quiet demeanor.
This singing contest ultimately concluded with multiple encore performances of "Oh-Woo-Oh!". Everyone had a wonderful time, and furthermore, once Jacinta's "true nature" became clear, the number of operators coming to hang out with her multiplied several times over.

handbook.char_4237_jcinta.story.5.text.text:
Rhodes Island's Medical Department recently secured a massive investment. With these funds, the Medical Department will have greater leeway to continue researching new drugs, expanding pharmaceutical production lines, and designing and upgrading medical equipment. However, no sum of money simply appears out of thin air:
Not long after Operator Jacinta joined Rhodes Island, a middle-aged couple accompanied by a group of rather menacing-looking men in black and a retinue of doctors carrying various medical devices paid a visit to Rhodes Island. Claiming to be Operator Jacinta's parents, Mr. and Mrs. Campbell, along with her bodyguard and medical team, they had come to visit Jacinta and intended to take charge of her living safety and treatment while at Rhodes Island.
And so, on that day, Operator Jacinta led her parents on a tour of the dormitories, wards, cafeteria, and other areas of her daily life. The Campbells not only showered her with endless instructions and warnings along the way regarding various issues, but also attempted to negotiate with HR to customize a specialized lifestyle, diet, travel, and treatment plan for Jacinta, prepare renovations for her dormitory, and confirm the missions she would undertake as well as her training intensity... Just as the accompanying HR operator was contemplating whether to step in and intervene, Operator Jacinta instead let out a fierce shout, halting her parents' endless stream of admonishments.
Contrary to the HR operator's worries, once Operator Jacinta presented proof of having passed her various training evaluations and mission authorization permits, the Campbells heeded their daughter's words, dismissed the bodyguard and medical team, and chose to trust and support the choices their daughter had made. Before leaving, however, they still wished to express their care for their daughter in their own way—thus, following a brief discussion, Rhodes Island's Medical Department suddenly received a substantial investment, usable for various medical research projects to better care for Operator Jacinta. Even better, upon learning that Rhodes Island's operations required massive energy support, the Campbells consulted with the Procurement Department regarding future mineral supply partnerships. Ensuring Rhodes Island possessed sufficient resources to take good care of their daughter, and confirming Jacinta could take care of herself, the Campbells finally departed for Rim Billiton, well-satisfied.
Jacinta was overjoyed. For all these years, aside from the sanatorium and the room at home that had been converted into a sickroom, she finally possessed a room of her own: it truly wasn't very large, nor were its facilities all that comprehensive, but this was the first room that belonged to her alone, one she could decorate however she pleased—and that also meant she and her parents had finally found a new dynamic for their relationship.
Of course, Kal'tsit and Closure—who had finally managed to score another business deal—were thrilled as well!

handbook.char_4237_jcinta.story.6.text.text:
Jacinta kept a calendar.
When she was five, Jacinta received her first calendar. That calendar wasn't bought by Jacinta herself; it was purchased by her parents when the doctor declared she wouldn't live past a month. Mr. and Mrs. Campbell densely jotted down the times for Jacinta's treatments, medication schedules, and commemorative trips... Yet that calendar was eventually thrown away by the Campbells, for the arduous experience exhausted them thoroughly; they only needed to see that Jacinta remained alive under their protection.
When she was ten, Jacinta bought a calendar for herself. To ensure her health, the Campbells sent her to a sanatorium and hired various personnel to oversee her studies, daily routine, and hobbies. Conversely, however, the busy Campbells could not frequently visit her, nor could the frail Jacinta leave the center for long periods to return home, so she bought a calendar to record the days her parents came to visit. That calendar was later thrown away by Jacinta as well; the days her parents came to see her grew fewer and fewer, and Jacinta felt she had no need to keep such records specifically.
At nineteen, Jacinta found a calendar in her attending physician's office. Unlike other calendars, this one was compiled from several years combined into one volume, every single page densely covered with precautions, while the final few pages were marked in gray. Jacinta knew those represented the doctor's estimations of her remaining time. That day, when she returned to her room, she wept bitterly, then made an identical calendar herself, tearing off one page as each day passed, watching it grow thinner and thinner, waiting for the day she would tear off the final page.
It wasn't as though she hadn't attempted to run away from the sanatorium before, but no one was willing to take a critical patient like her on the road, and her attempts and failures were merely insignificant little marks on a calendar. Until one day, Jacinta tore off a page out of habit, only to notice that the calendar had somehow dwindled down to a mere sliver.
Since she had already failed before, trying once more was no big deal. So, why not today? Jacinta pushed open the door and bolted.
From the day she ran out, Jacinta's calendar grew thicker and thicker. Every commemorative group photo, every map of places she had visited, even receipts from meals by the roadside and a tuft of shed fluff—she added them all in. When a day passed and she prepared to tear a page away, countless countless pages detailing the little moments of her life had already accumulated behind it.
Jacinta had a calendar, and this calendar was growing thicker by the day.

handbook.char_4237_jcinta.story.7.text.text:
After her treatment at Rhodes Island came to a close, Jacinta embarked on her journey.
Perhaps due to good fortune, or perhaps because Jacinta continually kept her and Amelia's entrepreneurial venture on her mind, she always seemed to find a way at the most unexpected moments to pitch their products.
While sightseeing in Sami, she lent a mobile signal base station originally brought along just for testing to a rescue team, successfully saving trapped personnel; shooting videos alongside Cutter, her likes and follower counts skyrocketed, attracting numerous media companies to reach out; even when preparing to scale a snow mountain alongside Aurora—limited by her physical condition, she ultimately made the wise choice to give up the climb—Jacinta crossed paths with Rhine Lab personnel, delivering Amelia's business card straight into the hands of the major Columbia corporation she admired, prompting a weeping Amelia to drop tears of joy every day upon receiving the news.
However, the events Jacinta encountered during her travels weren't solely tied to her and Amelia's business endeavors.
As an Oripathy patient, Jacinta knew certain matters were genuinely difficult to handle and resolve. That day at the foot of the snow mountain, Jacinta encountered someone clad in meager clothing. Originium crystals were spreading across that person's skin, every step tearing at flesh and oozing bloodstains; anyone could tell she was a severe patient. The snow mountain was merely an ordinary peak amid the snowfields, and nearby residents lived off it, gradually developing a faith of their own. Perhaps that person was here to offer prayers, but Jacinta knew this would yield no help, only causing irreversible damage to her health. The surrounding villagers told her that person had lost her mind and it was best to stay away; they never spoke to her at all.
She accompanied that person at the foot of the mountain for three days. Initially, Jacinta would constantly plead and persuade, attempting to share her medicines and food, helping her pitch a tent, and contacting Rhodes Island branch operators to seek aid, but the individual remained utterly silent. Discovering that the person's spirits were growing increasingly listless, Jacinta stopped trying to persuade her. She merely sat not far from the person, quietly keeping company, occasionally adding fuel to the fire before them so they both might be a bit more comfortable.
When the sun rose on the fourth day, the person's tent was empty; Jacinta found only a strip of bark inside the tent with a short line scrawled in ash: "Thank you for staying with me." Far away in a mountain cave, she found the traces left behind by the person's disintegration.
"At least she wasn't very lonely in the end..." Contrary to the medical operators' expectations, when speaking of this incident, Jacinta appeared very calm.

handbook.char_4237_jcinta.story.8.text.text:
......
We were narrow-minded. We never imagined you could be so brave. We thought letting you survive was enough, while ignoring your pain, and... ignoring our own pain.
I won't say too much in this letter lest you misunderstand; I only want to tell you—heaven knows how surprised we were when we received your photos from the Southern territories—you really did it!
Back at Big Iron Town, it was your mother who told me she had never seen you as happy as you were driving that night. I was half-in-clue at the time, thinking your mother was just coddling you... But when you were in the Southern territories, you looked genuinely happy. For a very, very long time since you fell ill, I hadn't seen you smile with such joy. Truly, for so long. That was my fault.
Our brave little one, our daughter, thank you for giving yourself a brand-new life, and thank you for giving me a chance to re-examine myself.
I'm sorry.
Thank you.
You will always be our pride.
— Your Father

handbook.char_1049_catap2.story.5.text.text:
When we get together, we often play competitive tabletop games.
The victor always seems to follow a certain rule—when everyone is still unfamiliar with the rules, Popukar usually wins the most. Once everyone has more or less figured out the rules, either Spot or I win the most.
Furthermore, the more Popukar wins at the beginning, the more miserably she loses later on. On one hand, this is because she is very skilled at using the rules to hinder others in order to win. Her victory is invariably built upon the misery of someone, or even several people, so she tends to face retaliation afterwards—sometimes off-the-board, like me assigning her some extra tasks. On the other hand, once the initial novelty wears off, she clearly loses interest in the game, and the rest of the time she is just playing along to keep us company.
This matches her general impression completely: three-minute enthusiasm, unwilling to spend too much time on anything. This kind of personality is not exactly rare. In other words, it ought to be a trait shared by many adolescents—possessing boundless vitality, yet having no idea where to pour their passion.
With the passage of time and an accumulation of life experience, most children either lose their vitality or find an object to pour their passion into. Popukar's peculiarity lies in the fact that, even at her age, she still retains her vitality and the distress of being unable to determine a goal... Well, actually, I don't think there is anything particularly special about that. If anything, self-proclaimed mature adults often just lose the passion for exploration and casually pick something random to treat as their goal.
As one of such adults, I mostly hate Popukar's childlike personality, much like when we play tabletop games—you can clearly sense in many things that she could do better, but she simply refuses to, and often causes me extra trouble because of it.
One could say that the only role time and experience play in her is making her clearly aware of the degree of responsibility she needs to bear for what she is doing. When she wants to find some fun from something she already finds boring, she knows what kind of trouble she causes is controllable, that it can be wrapped up just by me scolding her a couple of times. This often makes her look even more "detestable," but, sigh, what else can I do?
I say all this because I want to clarify one thing—ever since we returned from Sargon, quite a few colleagues feel that Popukar has changed, but from my perspective, Popukar has not changed at all.
Thank goodness, if I had to say what contribution this baffling journey to the Mirage Realm brought to Rhodes Island, I suppose it would only be that Popukar has finally found a toy she can't put down—and it seems she won't lose her enthusiasm for it for a very long time.
— "Additional Archival Records Regarding the Mirage Realm Incident"

handbook.char_4231_clemnt.story.6.text.text:
[A Complaint Letter, from Clementia's Physician]
You almost never see Clementia sleep.
Don't tell me that Aegirians don't need to follow the rising and setting of the sun; I am an Aegirian myself. The premise of freely deciding one's rest schedule is that the schedule at least includes a "rest" part.
I don't care why Clementia doesn't sleep; she always has a reason. If it's not because of her work as an Archon, it's excuses like "I faintly feel the login time of the data hub is half a second slower," or "The drainage sound of the airlock seems a little different from usual." In short, she's never at ease here, never letting go there. Every time she goes to find the person in charge regarding these matters, she stays for seven or eight hours. Afterwards, she would appear directly in the Archon's meditation chamber and continue her primary duties.
Understandably, Clementia's health condition is truly less than optimal. Even if my reminders weren't enough, Archon Heratia even specially equipped her with a customized little helper to remind her of this at any time. But most of the time, the health monitoring module of this little helper is turned off by her.
That's still not the worst part.
The worst part is when she occasionally actually decides to sleep. It is only then that she turns on the health monitoring module of the little helper. The little helper faithfully broadcasts her less-than-optimistic physical conditions to her—her bundle branch block, her fin tissue nodules... Archon Heratia said that, from a certain point onward, this has been the only way Clementia can fall asleep—listening to these broadcasts.
I don't understand. How can a person feel... at ease because of the deterioration of their own health condition? It's practically a provocation to medicine.

[A Research Record, from the Intelligent Machinery Design Institute]
The very moment the legion fleet returned, a malfunctioning little helper was sent to my laboratory. When the logistics module unloaded it, it was still using a clear, bright voice to faithfully broadcast the information it had collected from the battlefield:
"Agrippa, deceased, cause of death: crushed chest cavity caused by ship engine explosion.
"Flaminia, deceased, cause of death: nitrogen narcosis caused by diving armor damage.
"Paulinus, deceased, cause of death: acute malformation caused by Seaborn cell invasion."
Before the support fleet found the wreckage of that engineering mothership, it had spent seven days surrounded by a swarm of Seaborn. The only survivors rescued from it were a single survivor and this malfunctioning little helper. The little helper's logic components were severely damaged; it wouldn't obey commands, couldn't be operated, and couldn't even be shut down. Other than smashing its sound emitter with a hammer, I couldn't think of any way to make it quiet. It just repeated the information of every crew member over, and over, and over again: not only the news of the deaths of hundreds of colleagues and their respective causes of death, but also the injuries of that survivor, and... how many days she had left to live. After retrieving the data, it was discovered that it had repeated the broadcast one hundred and fifty-three times during those seven days. One doesn't need professional psychological knowledge to imagine how agonizing it must be to spend hundreds of consecutive hours listening to these death sentence broadcasts in such a small, confined space accompanied only by misshapen corpses.
When visiting that survivor, I asked her why she didn't destroy the sound emitter of this little helper, when she clearly had a sword in her hand.
She couldn't speak yet at the time, and simply wrote these words to me: "I've never seen a little helper malfunction like that. Don't you want to study it?"
I later heard that she stood guard in the cabin for a full seven days back then just to preserve a precious "primary" tissue sample. They awarded her an honorary title and made her a Legion Commander... But I can hardly imagine how she could view that as an honor.
